title: Recover from longhorn-storageclass ConfigMap YAML bug cascade
description: Overnight cascade: ansible task longhorn-storage-config.yml:87 wrote a literal '\n' (backslash-n) into ConfigMap longhorn-storageclass/storageclass.yaml. Longhorn-manager crashlooped on YAML parse error -> instance-manager ownership churn -> 15+ volumes faulted -> Vault lost quorum. ConfigMap patched. Recovery in progress.
notes: Root cause: ansible/roles/cluster_platform/tasks/longhorn-storage-config.yml:87 used Jinja2 "\n" which renders as literal backslash-n inside the JSON patch passed to kubectl. This corrupted the longhorn-storageclass ConfigMap data, crashing longhorn-manager which then triggered an instance-manager cascade and the worker-2 iSCSI corruption. Fix: remove the ~ "\n" concatenation (the Jinja \| block scalar already provides a trailing newline).

title: REGRESSION: dell-sff's nightly pbs-to-nas-1 vzdump job lost in the cluster join
description:
The pbs VM is currently NOT being backed up. dell-sff ran its own nightly vzdump of the PBS VM to nas-1 (schedule 21:00, storage nas-1, mode snapshot) -- backing up the backup server itself, which PBS cannot do into its own datastore. That job lived in dell-sff's /etc/pve/jobs.cfg, and the 2026-08-14 cluster join replaced dell-sff's entire /etc/pve with the cluster's copy, taking the job with it.

Evidence: /mnt/pve/nas-1/dump/vzdump-qemu-107-*.vma.zst exists for 2026-08-11, 08-12 and 08-13 at 21:00 (~6 GiB each, log confirms 'VM Name: pbs', disks on ssd2), and nothing after. The join happened ~23:37 on 08-13. The surviving cluster jobs.cfg has exactly one job (04:00 -> pbs storage) with no nas-1 target.

Note the guest is now VMID 147, not 107 -- pbs was renumbered during the join to clear a collision with atlas's k3s-prod-worker-gpu-1.
design:
This was a miss during the join: se6.3.7 correctly predicted /etc/pve replacement and storage.cfg + users + API tokens were all checked and repaired, but jobs.cfg was not on the checklist. Worth adding to the pre-join checklist for any future node (proliant-1): /etc/pve/jobs.cfg, /etc/pve/vzdump.cron, and any node-local firewall or replication config all live in the replaced tree.

Recreate the job with vmid 147 and storage nas-1. Retention needs confirming with Pierce -- only 3 daily backups were present, suggesting keep-last=3, but that could equally be a young job or an external prune. Do not guess silently.

Also worth deciding: should this move to the cluster-wide jobs.cfg (so it survives future /etc/pve churn and runs regardless of which node hosts pbs) rather than being recreated as a node-local job? pbs is on dellssf today but is a migration candidate like anything else now the cluster exists.
acceptance_criteria: A scheduled job backs up the pbs guest (VMID 147) to nas-1 again; a run completes successfully and a new vzdump-qemu-147-* appears in /mnt/pve/nas-1/dump/; retention explicitly set rather than inherited by accident.
notes: 2026-08-14 pbs has since been live-migrated from dellssf to elitedesk-1 (VMID still 147, 61ms downtime) to relieve dell-sff memory pressure -- see home-infra-qjmt. Does not change this issue: Proxmox backup jobs target guests by VMID cluster-wide, so the recreated job works regardless of which node hosts pbs. It does strengthen the argument in the design notes for defining it as a cluster-wide job in /etc/pve/jobs.cfg rather than a node-local one, since pbs has now demonstrably moved hosts once already.
close_reason:
Fixed 2026-08-14. Recreated as a CLUSTER-WIDE job in /etc/pve/jobs.cfg (id ddb1d259-cdce-477e-bded-5894af867871) rather than node-local, so it survives both future /etc/pve churn and pbs moving hosts -- which it already did once tonight, dellssf -> elitedesk-1.

Settings, matched to the lost job except retention: vmid 147, storage nas-1, schedule 21:00, mode snapshot, compress zstd, notes-template {{guestname}}, notification-mode notification-system. The original's retention was confirmed from its own log ('prune older backups with retention: keep-last=3') rather than guessed; deliberately raised to keep-last=7 to match the other cluster job and give a week of recovery window. At ~5.8 GB per archive that is ~41 GB against 14.3 TiB free on nas-1.

Verified by an actual run, not just config: 32 GiB read in 67s (489 MiB/s), 28% sparse, archive 5.79 GB, completed in 1m19s, vzdump-qemu-147-* now present on nas-1.

Side effect worth noting: adding 147 to the new job removed it from the 04:00 pbs-storage job's vmid list. That is the desired arrangement -- pbs no longer backs itself up into its own datastore, which was circular, and now goes only to nas-1.

title: DECISION: which host owns the cluster -- flip join direction so atlas creates 'oasis'?
description:
se6.3.1 settled that reusing the 'oasis' identity is fine, and the plan since then assumed that means atlas + elitedesk-1 join dell-sff (the host that currently carries oasis). Given se6.3.5 (the joining node must be emptied of guests), that assumption is now the expensive one and should be re-tested.

Emptying cost by host:
- atlas: 16 guests, including the ENTIRE prod k3s control plane (cp-1/2/3), 3 workers, the GPU worker, warpgate, mint-vm. Worst possible node to empty.
- dell-sff: 10 guests, including technitium (network DNS), haos (3 USB dongles), caddy, wg-easy, guacamole, pbs.
- elitedesk-1: 3 guests -- cp-4, worker-4, and a duplicate template that is being deleted anyway (se6.3.6). Cheapest by far.
design:
The key realisation: the 'oasis' name is not tied to dell-sff. 'pvecm create oasis' on atlas reproduces the identity Pierce said he wanted to keep, and pvecm create has NO empty-node precondition -- only pvecm add does. So the name can be preserved while flipping which host does the joining.

Option A (as previously planned): dell-sff stays the cluster; atlas and elitedesk-1 join.
  -> atlas must be emptied of 16 guests incl. all prod etcd members. Also inverts se6.3.6 so the renumbering lands on atlas's Terraform/Ansible-tracked k3s VMs. Not recommended.

Option B (flip): atlas runs 'pvecm create oasis'; elitedesk-1 joins, dell-sff joins later.
  -> dell-sff must first be de-clustered (its single-node oasis torn down) and emptied of 10 guests, incl. network DNS.
  -> elitedesk-1 is cheap: 3 guests, one of which is deleted anyway.

Option C (phased B, recommended): atlas creates oasis, elitedesk-1 joins now. That is a real 2-node cluster achieved with the cheapest possible emptying, and it directly unblocks moving CP presence off atlas. Defer dell-sff's join to its own change window, since its 10 guests include network DNS and it is the fiddliest.
  -> Caveat: 2 nodes cannot tolerate a failure without a tie-breaker, which raises the priority of se6.3.3 (nas-1 QDevice) from 'needed before proliant-1' to 'needed as soon as the cluster is even-numbered'.
  -> Caveat: se6.8 (live-migrate cp-3 atlas -> dell-sff) stays blocked until dell-sff actually joins. Under option C the near-term CP spread would instead have to target elitedesk-1, which already hosts cp-4 -- so it may not help CP spread at all until dell-sff lands. Worth thinking through with Pierce before committing to the phasing.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit decision from Pierce on cluster owner and phasing, recorded here, before se6.3.4 runs any pvecm command.
close_reason: Pierce decided 2026-08-14: FLIP the direction. atlas runs 'pvecm create oasis' (keeps the oasis identity, and create has no empty-node precondition so atlas's 16 guests are never disturbed). elitedesk-1 joins now -- cheapest node to empty at 3 guests, one of which is a duplicate template being deleted anyway. dell-sff de-clusters and joins in a LATER window, because its 10 guests include network DNS (technitium) and haos with USB passthrough. Accepted consequences: (1) se6.8 (live-migrate cp-3 atlas -> dell-sff) stays blocked until that second window, so CP spread off atlas does not advance yet; (2) the interim cluster is 2 nodes = even, so nas-1 QDevice (se6.3.3) is promoted from 'needed before proliant-1' to 'needed for the interim cluster'.

title: BLOCKER: 5 VMID collisions across the three hosts must be resolved before clustering
description:
VMIDs are globally unique across a Proxmox cluster and shared between VMs and CTs. Inventory taken 2026-08-14:

atlas   VMs 100,101,102,103,104,105,107,301,302,9000,9001,9999 | CTs 201,1000,9100,9101
dellssf VMs 101,107 | CTs 100,102,106,115,120,121,124,126
elite-1 VMs 108,111,9000

Collisions:
- 100: atlas VM k3s-prod-cp-3    <-> dell-sff CT technitium
- 101: atlas VM k3s-prod-worker-1 <-> dell-sff VM haos
- 102: atlas VM k3s-prod-cp-2    <-> dell-sff CT cloudflare
- 107: atlas VM k3s-prod-worker-gpu-1 <-> dell-sff VM pbs
- 9000: atlas debian12-server-template <-> elitedesk-1 debian12-server-template
design:
Renumbering is not just a config rename -- LVM/ZFS volume names embed the VMID (vm-<id>-disk-N), so each renumber touches the config AND the backing volumes. Cheapest assignment given the goal is to keep atlas untouched:

- 9000 on elitedesk-1: it is a rebuildable Packer template and duplicates atlas's. Delete it rather than renumber.
- The four dell-sff collisions (100,101,102,107) renumber on the dell-sff side, since atlas's are prod k3s nodes referenced by Terraform state and Ansible inventory. Note dell-sff 101=haos carries 3 USB passthrough dongles and 107=pbs is the backup server -- both need care.
- If the join direction ends up flipping so atlas is the one joining, this assignment inverts and gets much more expensive (Terraform state + Ansible inventory churn). Another reason direction matters.
acceptance_criteria: No VMID appears on more than one host; renumbered guests boot with their disks correctly attached.
notes:
2026-08-14 scope narrowed by the se6.3.8 flip: atlas is now the cluster CREATOR and never joins, so its VMIDs are fixed points and none of its guests get renumbered -- the Terraform/Ansible churn risk is gone. For the elitedesk-1 join the only live collision is 9000 (atlas debian12-server-template vs elitedesk-1's duplicate) -- resolve by DELETING elitedesk-1's copy, since atlas's will become cluster-visible anyway. The four dell-sff collisions (100 technitium, 101 haos, 102 cloudflare, 107 pbs) all still stand and must be renumbered on the dell-sff side, but they are deferred to dell-sff's own join window.
2026-08-14 CORRECTION -- do NOT delete elitedesk-1's 9000 template. Checked the storage: atlas's 9000 lives on 'tank' (zfspool, nodes atlas) and elitedesk-1's on 'local-lvm'. Neither is shared storage, and 'qm clone --target <node>' is only permitted when the source is on shared storage -- so elitedesk-1 cannot clone from atlas's template across the cluster and genuinely needs a local one. They are not even the same build (8G disk on atlas vs 3G on elitedesk-1).

Second half of the collision that VMID-only thinking misses: both templates are also NAMED 'debian12-server-template', and terraform/stacks/k3s/elitedesk-1/prod/{control-plane,workers}/main.tf clone BY NAME (telmate provider, clone = var.template_name) against elitedesk-1's own API endpoint. Post-join that endpoint sees the whole cluster, so the name lookup becomes ambiguous. Both the ID and the name must be made unique.

Plan: elitedesk-1's template config gets moved aside with the other guests anyway, so restore it post-join as VMID 9002 -- lvrename base-9000-disk-0 -> base-9002-disk-0 and vm-9000-cloudinit -> vm-9002-cloudinit, edit the disk refs, and set name: debian12-server-template-elitedesk-1. Then update template_name in the two elitedesk-1 stacks. cp-4/worker-4 were full_clone=true so nothing depends on the thin base volume. Not urgent for this session -- both VMs already exist; the template only matters for future provisioning.
2026-08-14 the 9000 collision is RESOLVED. elitedesk-1's template was renumbered to 9002 in the post-join restore: lvrename pve/base-9000-disk-0 -> base-9002-disk-0 and pve/vm-9000-cloudinit -> vm-9002-cloudinit (verified no thin-snapshot origins depended on it, since cp-4/worker-4 were full_clone=true), config restored as 9002.conf with name debian12-server-template-elitedesk-1. Committed 6f7f0ab4 updates template_name in both elitedesk-1 stacks. Remaining scope is only the four dell-sff collisions (100/101/102/107), now blocking se6.3.9.
close_reason: All 5 VMID collisions resolved 2026-08-14. 9000 (atlas vs elitedesk-1 template) fixed during the elitedesk-1 join by renumbering to 9002. The four dell-sff collisions fixed during its join: 100 technitium->140, 101 haos->141, 102 cloudflare->142, 107 pbs->147. Verified via pvesh get /cluster/resources: 28 guests cluster-wide, zero duplicate VMIDs. dell-sff's non-colliding IDs (106/115/120/121/124/126) were deliberately left alone per surgical-change discipline.

title: BLOCKER: pvecm add refuses nodes that have any guests -- reshapes se6.3.4
description: Verified 2026-08-14 in PVE 9 source on atlas: PVE/Cluster/Setup.pm:639 assert_joinable() hard-fails with 'this host already contains virtual guests' if the joining node has ANY VM or CT config. All three hosts currently have guests (atlas 12 VMs + 4 CTs, dell-sff 2 VMs + 8 CTs, elitedesk-1 3 VMs), so se6.3.4 as written (join atlas + elitedesk-1 into dell-sff's oasis) cannot execute as-is.
design:
--force exists but bypasses the check rather than solving it: joining replaces the node's /etc/pve with the cluster's copy, so the joining node's guest configs would vanish (disks survive on LVM/ZFS, configs do not). Not acceptable to improvise on atlas's 16 running guests.

Two viable shapes:
(a) Move-aside: stop guests, back up /etc/pve/qemu-server/*.conf + /etc/pve/lxc/*.conf off-host, remove them, pvecm add, restore configs into the cluster's node dir, start guests. Disks never touched. Downtime = guest stop duration.
(b) vzdump to NFS/PBS, destroy guests, join, qmrestore. Bulletproof rollback, but full data copy.

Either way the emptying burden falls on the JOINING node, which is why join direction now matters -- see the direction decision issue.
acceptance_criteria: Chosen approach recorded and the guest-precondition step is explicit in se6.3.4's plan before any pvecm command runs.
notes: 2026-08-14 Pierce chose the move-aside method: stop guests, back up /etc/pve/qemu-server/*.conf and /etc/pve/lxc/*.conf off-host, remove them so assert_joinable() passes, pvecm add, restore the configs into the cluster's /etc/pve/nodes/<node>/ dir, start guests. Backing disks on LVM/ZFS are never touched; downtime is bounded by the guest stop duration. vzdump/qmrestore rejected as a full data copy that buys rollback we get more cheaply from an off-host config backup.
close_reason: Resolved in practice 2026-08-14. The precondition is real and was handled with the move-aside method on elitedesk-1: drain -> qm shutdown -> save configs off-host -> rm from /etc/pve -> pvecm add -> restore configs -> qm start. Total guest downtime ~12 minutes, zero data touched (all backing LVM volumes intact and verified before/after). The same procedure applies unchanged to the deferred dell-sff join -- see the dell-sff join issue. Captured durably in the 'pvecm-add-requires-empty-node' bd memory.

title: Build dedicated health-archive ingester service (multi-format)
description:
Replace the n8n Health Sync Daily Import CSV parsing with a purpose-built, GitOps-managed ingester.

Root causes found in the n8n workflow:
1. Drive query filters 'name contains Health Connect' -> Sleep/Weight/Activities files (Samsung-named + workout exports) are never listed.
2. Parser is Health-Connect-CSV-only: Samsung Health files yielded 311 observations across 923 files (921 produced zero); workout exports (.csv/.tcx/.gpx/.kml/.fit) produced 0 across 328 files.

4. Determine Recovery Cutoff only considers source_name='Health Sync / Health Connect'; folders with no HC data fall back to a rolling today-30d floor, permanently preventing historical backfill.

Target: Python service in repo, per-format parsers (Health Connect CSV, Samsung Health CSV, workout CSV, TCX/GPX XML, FIT binary), same Postgres contract (health_sources / health_observations_raw / health_ingested_files, ON CONFLICT (source_id, original_type, external_id)), Prometheus metrics + per-metric staleness alerting via existing Alertmanager/ntfy.

Sources to cover: Zepp watch, Samsung ring (via Samsung Health), FitBod workouts, all bridged through Health Connect/Health Sync.
close_reason: Shipped. Root cause was two layers of loss in the n8n workflow: a Drive query requiring 'Health Connect' in the filename, and a selector requiring exactly one date token and a 'Health Connect.csv' suffix. Samsung-named, week-numbered and date-range exports plus all workout files were dropped before parsing. title: Memos volume replica flapping on worker nodes
description:
## Memos Volume Replica Flapping on Worker Nodes

### Root Cause
The memos-data-v3 Longhorn replica process crashes with SIGBUS (bus error) on workers 1 and 3 within 4ms of startup. Only memos is affected — all other volumes' replicas run fine on the same disks. Most likely a Longhorn v1.11.2 bug with restored-from-backup volumes that have `Dirty: true` metadata.

### Workaround (Active)
- Volume pinned to worker-2 via `nodeSelector: [k3s-prod-worker-2]`
- `replicaSoftAntiAffinity: enabled` and `replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity: enabled` on the volume
- Both replicas on worker-2's single flash disk — volume is `healthy`

### Worker-3 Overcommit Fix (Active)
- `storage-over-provisioning-percentage` set to 110% (was 150%) — prevents new scheduling on overcommitted disks
- `replica-auto-balance-disk-pressure-percentage` set to 45% (was 90%) — triggers best-effort rebalancing when disk usage exceeds 55%
- Worker-3 is now marked unschedulable (DiskPressure) — no new replicas land there
- Both settings added to Ansible for consistency across deploys

### Follow-up
1. File Longhorn bug for SIGBUS on restored-from-backup volume replica creation
2. Once bug is fixed, remove nodeSelector from memos volume and let replicas spread
3. Monitor worker-3 gradual rebalancing over time as pods cycle

title: Protect pve/data thin pool from re-fill (autoextend + alerts)
description:
The Proxmox host `atlas` runs every cluster VM's OS disk on a single 337 GiB LVM thin pool `pve/data` on the (healthy) Samsung 860 EVO /dev/sde3. The pool itself is overprovisioned: sum of thin volume sizes (440 GiB) > pool size (337 GiB).

On 2026-05-20 the pool filled to 100% data utilization when a ~30 GiB LLM model was downloaded into a VM's home directory (an attempt to work around the temporarily-missing ssd3 — see home-infra-sbd; ssd3's disappearance was a faulty SATA adapter, not a drive failure). All VMs entered Proxmox `io-error` state; k3s nodes cp-3 and worker-3 went NotReady; the in-progress Plex PVC migration was killed mid-flight at ~92%.

Recovery required:
1. `lvextend -L+15G /dev/pve/data` (consuming the 16 GiB of unallocated VG headroom)
2. `qm unlock` + `qm stop` + `qm start` on the prelaunch-stuck VMs (cp-3=vm-100, worker-3=vm-105)
3. Restarting the Plex rsync sidecar (which resumed from its partial copy)

After the extend, the pool is at 88.98% with only 1 GiB of unallocated VG space remaining. The root issue is overcommit without observability — the drive is fine, but a single large write in any VM can fill the shared pool again.
design:
Three layers of defense, applied in order:

LAYER 1 — make LVM auto-respond to high-water marks (`/etc/lvm/lvm.conf` on atlas):
  thin_pool_autoextend_threshold = 80
  thin_pool_autoextend_percent   = 10
This only delays, it doesn't fix root cause: pve VG has only 1 GiB free, so autoextend has nowhere to grow. Still worth setting for the day we add capacity.

LAYER 2 — observability so we are paged before re-fill:
  - node-exporter textfile collector script on atlas: scrape `lvs --noheadings -o lv_name,data_percent --units b` and emit `node_lvm_thin_pool_data_percent{vg,pool}` metrics
  - PrometheusRule alert: `node_lvm_thin_pool_data_percent{pool="data"} > 85` for 15m → critical
  - Add to existing alertmanager ntfy-prod-critical route

LAYER 3 — eliminate the root cause:
  - VM 107's home directory should NEVER hold model files. Either bind-mount a dedicated disk for downloads, or document strict policy.
  - Long-term: move VM OS disks off the shared thin pool entirely (per-VM dedicated LVs or move to ZFS).
acceptance_criteria:
- `/etc/lvm/lvm.conf` on atlas has `thin_pool_autoextend_threshold` set to a value below 100 (managed via Ansible role `common` or new role `proxmox_host_lvm`)
- A node-exporter textfile or dedicated exporter publishes `node_lvm_thin_pool_data_percent` for `pve/data`
- A PrometheusRule fires at >85% sustained 15m through ntfy-prod-critical
- Operations runbook (`docs/operations/cluster-operations.md`) documents recovery procedure (lvextend, unstick prelaunch VMs, restart any in-flight rsync)
- Documented policy on where it is safe to land large files on cluster VMs (i.e. not `~/`, not `/var/log`, etc.)

Root cause confirmed: k3s VM scsi0 disks (on local-lvm/pve/data) were created without discard=on. Guest fstrim was a no-op at the thin-pool layer.

Procedure that worked, per VM:
  qm set <vmid> --scsi0 local-lvm:vm-<vmid>-disk-0,discard=on,<other-options>
  qm reboot <vmid>
  # wait Ready
  ansible -i ... <host> -m shell -a 'fstrim -av' -b

CP rollout this session (cp-1 vm-104, cp-2 vm-102, cp-3 vm-100):
  - 30 GiB trimmed cp-1, 18 GiB cp-2, 30 GiB cp-3 = ~78 GiB cleared
  - pve/data 97.55 → 89.75 → 84.87 → 77.99
  - ProxmoxThinPoolDataHigh alert should clear (threshold 85%)

Workers still needed (vm-101=worker-1, vm-103=worker-2, vm-105=worker-3, vm-107=worker-gpu-1). Each requires:
  1. kubectl cordon + drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
  2. qm set discard=on + qm reboot
  3. wait Ready, fstrim
  4. kubectl uncordon
Estimated 10-15 min per worker; gpu-1 lowest-risk first because it has fewest replicas. Schedule in a maintenance window.

Long-term protection (the issue's original scope):
  - Add lvm.conf thin_pool_autoextend_threshold + percent settings on atlas via ansible
  - Add discard=on to terraform/modules/proxmox-cloudinit-nodes module so future VMs ship with it
2026-08-14 the risk has MOVED HOSTS and this issue needs rescoping from atlas-only to all three cluster nodes. Measured tonight:

  atlas       pool 352.86g at 14.48%  VG free 1.00g   autoextend CONFIGURED (threshold 85, percent 20)
  elitedesk-1 pool 348.82g at 75.40%  VG free 16.00g  autoextend NOT configured
  dellssf     pool  53.93g at 31.67%  VG free 14.75g  autoextend NOT configured

Two distinct problems now:

1. atlas is no longer the danger (14.48%, workloads having moved to the tank/flash ZFS pools), BUT its autoextend config is effectively DEAD -- thin_pool_autoextend_threshold=85 with only 1.00g of unallocated VG left means the trigger fires and then has almost nothing to extend into. The protection reads as present but is not.

2. elitedesk-1 has inherited exactly the failure shape this issue describes, and has no autoextend at all. It climbed 57.3% -> 64.6% -> 75.4% in a single day (2026-08-14) as caddy/guacamole/wg-easy/cloudflare, then pbs and bambu-connect were migrated onto it. k3s-prod-worker-4's Longhorn disk (200G provisioned, ~155G actual) dominates it and grows on its own. It has a single 476.9G NVMe with no spare disks, so 16.00g is the entire ceiling for autoextend.

This is the same overcommit-without-observability pattern that took atlas down on 2026-05-20 (all VMs io-error, cp-3 and worker-3 NotReady, Plex migration killed at 92%). The consequence is now worse, because after tonight's control-plane redistribution each host carries an etcd member -- elitedesk-1 filling its pool would take cp-4 with it.

Alerting still does not exist on any host. Suggested scope: set autoextend on all three, make sure each has meaningful VG headroom to extend INTO (atlas currently does not), and add an actual alert on thin pool data_percent rather than relying on noticing. See also home-infra-se6.4 (disk allocation across hosts) which is the structural fix for elitedesk-1's single-disk constraint.

title: Model the physical topology in NetBox DCIM
description: Replace the hand-maintained Obsidian topology note and the repo's duplicated port tables with NetBox as the single source of truth for the physical network. NetBox was already load-bearing for DNS (netbox-technitium-sync drives levangie.org from each IP's dns_name), but its DCIM side was a stub: 7 devices with one placeholder eth0 each, zero cables, zero racks, and neither switch modelled.
design:
Populated via the REST API against netbox.levangie.dev (NetBox 4.2.4). Key safety decision: the placeholder eth0 interfaces were RENAMED IN PLACE (atlas/elitedesk-1/dellssf eth0 -> vmbr0 as type bridge, nas-1 eth0 -> bond0 as type lag) rather than creating new interfaces and moving the IPs across. That keeps every ipam/ip-addresses object and its dns_name untouched, so the Technitium sync could not produce DNS churn.

New cable runs are status=planned, existing links are status=connected, so NetBox doubles as the cabling checklist - flip each to connected as it is physically made.
acceptance_criteria: Both switches modelled with 8 ports each; real interfaces on all hosts with LAG and bridge relationships; 11 cables; all IPs and dns_name values unchanged.
close_reason: NetBox DCIM populated 2026-08-14 via the REST API. Added: device roles Switch and Workstation; device types for both switches and a generic workstation; devices sw-core-25g, sw-edge-1g, workstation-1; 16 switch ports; real interfaces on atlas (nic0/nic1/nic2/bond0/vmbr0), elitedesk-1 (enx6c1ff7cc61a4/nic0/bond0/vmbr0), dellssf (enx6c1ff7c0d19c/enp1s0/bond0/vmbr0) and nas-1 (lan1/lan2/bond0); LAG and bridge relationships on all of them; and 11 cables (4 connected, 7 planned). title: Add ProxmoxHostBondDegraded + ProxmoxHostLinkBelowExpected alerts
description:
Active-backup bonding exists specifically to hide a NIC failure. Without an alert, a dead USB adapter means silently running on the 1G standby leg for weeks with no signal. This is the most important follow-up in the epic.

Add two rules to argocd/manifests/monitoring-config/base/prometheusrule-platform.yaml alongside the existing ProxmoxThinPoolDataHigh (same node_exporter source, same pattern).
design:
1. ProxmoxHostBondDegraded: node_bonding_slaves - node_bonding_active > 0 for 5m.
2. ProxmoxHostLinkBelowExpected: node_network_speed_bytes{device="bond0"} < 312500000 for 10m (2.5 Gb/s = 312,500,000 B/s). Catches a link that renegotiated down to 1G - 2.5GBASE-T is fussy and marginal cabling is the usual cause.

Verified: node_exporter on the hosts already exposes node_network_speed_bytes (confirmed live against 172.20.20.7:9100), and the bonding collector is on by default, so node_bonding_* will populate once bond0 exists.
acceptance_criteria: Both rules present, ArgoCD synced, and evaluating without error in Prometheus once bond0 exists on at least one host.
close_reason: Both alerts committed in c69d68d2, synced by ArgoCD, and verified evaluating in prod Prometheus with health=ok, state=inactive, no errors. Scoped to job="proxmox-node-exporter" after confirming the live label set (instance=atlas/dellssf/elitedesk-1). Inert until bond0 exists, as intended.

title: NAS: verify switch LAG, convert Balance XOR -> 802.3ad LACP, add nconnect
description:
The DS420+ bond is in Balance XOR, which is a STATIC LAG and requires a matching static trunk on the 2.5G managed switch. Verify that trunk exists - if it was never configured, the switch is currently seeing one MAC (90:09:d0:23:02:89) on two ports and MAC-flapping, which is silent packet loss being lived with today.

Then convert both sides to 802.3ad LACP (more robust: detects miswiring and half-failures that static XOR silently tolerates), set the switch LAG hash to layer3+4, and add nconnect=4 to the Proxmox nas-1 NFS storage.
design:
Throughput model - be clear-eyed, the DS420+ is a 2x1G device and stays one. The 2.5G upgrade does NOT make the NAS faster for a single stream.

READS (NAS -> host): the NAS bond picks the egress link and DSM does not expose xmit_hash_policy, so it hashes on MAC pairs. Every conversation with a given host is pinned to one 1G link. Reads stay ~1 Gb/s per host, permanently.

WRITES (host -> NAS): the SWITCH picks the LAG member. With a layer3+4 hash and multiple TCP connections (hence nconnect=4), writes can spread across both links, up to ~2 Gb/s.

NFS is already vers=4.1 with rsize/wsize=131072, which supports nconnect. Edit the nas-1 entry in /etc/pve/storage.cfg.
acceptance_criteria: Switch LAG confirmed present and in LACP mode with layer3+4 hash; DSM bond shows 802.3ad; nconnect=4 active on all three hosts' nas-1 mount; write throughput measured before/after.

title: Cable + bond elitedesk-1
description:
Cable the already-seated RTL8156B (enx6c1ff7cc61a4) to the 2.5G switch, cable onboard nic0 to the 1G switch, convert vmbr0 onto active-backup bond0.

Highest-value host in this epic: it carries cp-4 (etcd), worker-4 (Longhorn replicas), pbs, and caddy (ALL public ingress). Its 1G link is the single biggest bottleneck in the lab.

Note: bd home-infra-mi4 recorded the USB NIC as enx0c37965cbfe2 but the adapter present on 2026-08-14 is enx6c1ff7cc61a4. Confirm which adapter is which before cabling.
design:
Slaves: enx6c1ff7cc61a4 (primary) + nic0 (standby). vmbr0 address 172.20.20.7/22.

Keep the existing nic0 post-up lines (tso/gso/gro off, EEE off - the I219 hang workaround).

GOTCHA: bonding ANDs netdev features across slaves, so nic0's disabled TSO/GSO/GRO may propagate to bond0 and cost CPU on the 2.5G path. Check 'ethtool -k bond0' after creating it. If TSO is off and throughput disappoints, either accept it (i5-12500 has ample headroom) or re-test whether the I219 workaround is still needed on kernel 7.0.
acceptance_criteria: 2500Mb/s link; bond0 active-backup healthy; failover verified; caddy-served public sites stay reachable after the change; ethtool -k bond0 offload state recorded.
notes: 2026-08-14: adapter identity mystery resolved by the user - enx0c37965cbfe2 was a separate 1G USB NIC used for testing, not one of the 2.5G units. The correct 2.5G adapter on elitedesk-1 is enx6c1ff7cc61a4 (Realtek RTL8156B, 0bda:8156). No ambiguity remains.

title: Cable + bond dellssf (first host, lowest blast radius)
description:
Insert the RTL8156B USB adapter into dellssf (currently NOT inserted - only enp1s0 exists), cable it to the 2.5G switch, cable enp1s0 to the 1G switch, and convert vmbr0 onto an active-backup bond0.

Guests affected while the link bounces: cp-3 (etcd member), haos, technitium, affirm-srv, gamble-king.

WARNING: technitium is the lab DNS server. Confirm a fallback resolver before this window or name resolution breaks lab-wide while dellssf is down.

Requires console access to the host. A bad /etc/network/interfaces makes it unreachable with no remote rollback.

title: (EPIC) 2.5G re-network: USB NIC cabling, host bonding, NAS LACP
description:
Cable the two Realtek RTL8156B USB 2.5GbE adapters onto the 2.5G managed switch and put all three Proxmox hosts on active-backup bonds (2.5G primary / onboard 1G standby), with the previously-idle 1G switch serving as the failover plane. Also converts the Synology bond from static Balance XOR to 802.3ad LACP.

Targets three bottlenecks: Longhorn cross-host replica rebuilds, Proxmox live migration, and PBS backups. elitedesk-1 and dellssf are currently the only 1G links in an otherwise 2.5G-capable lab.

Approved plan: ~/.claude/plans/i-have-received-my-lexical-waterfall.md
design:
Topology: 2.5G managed switch (8p) = atlas nic0, elitedesk-1 USB, dellssf USB, NAS LAN1+LAN2 (LAG), PC, uplink to 1G switch, 1 spare. 1G unmanaged switch (8p) = uplink, router (moved here), three onboard NICs as bond standby legs, 3 free for ProLiant.

Router moves to the 1G switch because its LAN port is 1G and can never exceed that regardless of switch, so the 1G uplink costs zero throughput and frees a 2.5G port.

Flat L2 172.20.20.0/22 retained. No VLANs, no jumbo frames (partial MTU 9000 on a flat subnet blackholes traffic; the NAS 1G ceiling makes the payoff near zero).

Bond config is ifupdown2 active-backup: bond-primary=USB, bond-primary-reselect always, miimon 100, downdelay 200, updelay 30000, num-grat-arp 5. USB names are MAC-derived and stable via /usr/lib/systemd/network/73-usb-net-by-mac.link.

Deliberately NOT automated in Ansible: one-time change on three hosts, and a bad rewrite of /etc/network/interfaces makes a host unreachable with no remote rollback.
acceptance_criteria: All three hosts show 2500Mb/s on their primary bond slave; bond failover verified per host with <1s traffic loss; iperf3 atlas<->elitedesk-1 reaches ~2.3-2.4 Gb/s vs the 917-932 Mb/s baseline; cluster stays quorate throughout.

title: Decommission k3s-prod-worker-3 from atlas
description:
Pierce raised this again on 2026-08-14: 'I may even remove one more prod worker VM from atlas.' It was also flagged in the Hardware Expansion handoff back on 2026-08-13 as pending-but-not-bd-tracked, alongside cp-3 -- and the cp-3 half has since been resolved differently (live-migrated to dellssf rather than destroyed, see home-infra-se6.8), leaving worker-3 as the remaining piece.

atlas currently carries ALL FOUR non-CP prod workers (worker-1, worker-2, worker-3, worker-gpu-1) plus cp-1, on a 56-thread / 314 GiB Xeon at load ~27-34. It is not short of capacity; the argument is failure-domain concentration, not resource pressure.
design:
The original gating condition was 'once the storage crisis is properly resolved, not just patched'. Longhorn has since converged (100 volumes healthy on 2026-08-14) and the cross-pool migration landed in June, so that gate is arguably met -- but check home-infra-mi4 first, because removing an atlas worker changes replica placement.

CRITICAL sequencing: worker-3 holds Longhorn replicas. Draining and destroying it forces rebuilds elsewhere. Right now the only non-atlas worker is worker-4 on elitedesk-1, whose thin pool is already at 75% (see the elitedesk-1-storage-constrained memory). Displaced replicas would have nowhere good to land. Strongly consider adding worker capacity off atlas FIRST -- home-infra-se6.7 is the placeholder for that, though dell-sff was ruled out as too weak, leaving elitedesk-1 (needs disk, see se6.4) or proliant-1 (not racked, se6.2).

Mechanics when the time comes: kubectl drain, remove from k3s, then Terraform destroy from terraform/stacks/k3s/atlas/prod/workers/ by dropping the list-tail entry (note the atlas CP stack's count-based indexing trap documented in home-infra-se6.8 -- verify the workers stack has the same shape before touching vm_count). Then remove from ansible/inventories/production/hosts.yml and update NetBox.
acceptance_criteria: worker-3 removed from k3s, its VM destroyed, Terraform state and the Ansible inventory reflect reality, and no Longhorn volume is left degraded or single-copy as a result.

title: Longhorn replica-auto-balance still 'disabled' since the 2026-05 recovery
description:
replica-auto-balance is still set to 'disabled' cluster-wide. It was turned off during the 2026-05-29 Longhorn cascade recovery as a deliberate temporary measure (to stop rebuilds reading bad LBAs off the failing flash drive and triggering SIGBUS in the engine), and the handoff at the time listed re-enabling it to 'best-effort' as a cleanup step. That never happened -- confirmed still 'disabled' on 2026-08-14, roughly two and a half months later.

Surfaced while retiring the stale handoff docs in handoff/; the original note was in 2026-05-29-longhorn-cross-pool-resilience.md item 5, which referenced no bd issue.
design:
The condition that justified disabling it is long gone -- the failing drive was swapped and the cross-pool migration completed back in May/June. Leaving auto-balance off means Longhorn will not redistribute replicas after node additions or removals, which matters much more now than it did in May: the cluster gained k3s-prod-worker-4 on elitedesk-1, lost cp-2, and moved cp-3 to dellssf, all on 2026-08-14. Replica placement has had no automatic rebalancing across any of that.

Decide between 'best-effort' (the pre-incident value) and 'least-effort', then set it via the Helm values path rather than kubectl patch -- see home-infra-zdc, which exists precisely because these settings drift when patched imperatively.

Sequencing note: this interacts with home-infra-mi4 (cross-host zone spread). Enabling auto-balance while zone labels are still unset (home-infra-mi4.1) means it rebalances without zone awareness. Probably worth doing mi4.1 first so the rebalancing it triggers is the kind you want.
acceptance_criteria: replica-auto-balance set to an explicitly chosen value, applied through Helm values rather than a kubectl patch, with the resulting replica movement observed and sane.

title: Clean up stale Proxmox backups: PBS datastore + nas-1 /dump
description:
Two separate backup stores have accumulated years of dead backups. Measured 2026-08-14:

PBS datastore (pbs VM, 172.20.20.22, datastore on nas-1) -- 281 snapshots total, logical size pre-dedup:
  2024: 100 snapshots, 2254.9 GiB
  2025:  38 snapshots,  489.8 GiB
  2026: 143 snapshots, 3523.9 GiB
  older than 1 year: 132 snapshots across 34 distinct guest IDs

nas-1 NFS /dump (vzdump files, separate from PBS) -- 72 GiB total:
  2023: 869 files, 54.4 GiB   <-- the bulk of the dead weight
  2024:   2 files,  ~0 GiB
  2026:   9 files, 17.1 GiB   <-- current, keep (3 nightly pbs backups)

The 2023 nas-1 files and the pre-2025 PBS snapshots are from the old pve1/pve2/pve3 'oasis' era and reference guests that no longer exist (119, 127, 202, 221, 230, 310, 350, 351, 900, 1001, 1002, 5555, 8000-8003, 8100 and others).
design:
CRITICAL CAVEAT -- do NOT prune by VMID. VMIDs have been recycled across the homelab's history, so several old-guest IDs are in active use by completely different guests today: 101 (now k3s-prod-worker-1), 102 (was cp-2, since destroyed), 108 (now k3s-prod-worker-4), 115 (now guacamole), 120 (now caddy), 130/131/132, 301 (now proxyd), 304, 350. Deleting 'all backups for VMID 115' would take out current guacamole backups alongside a dead 2023 guest. Prune by DATE, or verify each snapshot's guest identity before removing.

Suggested approach:
1. nas-1 /dump is the easy 54 GiB -- plain files, delete by mtime older than ~1 year after eyeballing the list. Keep the 2026 pbs backups.
2. PBS needs 'proxmox-backup-client'/GUI prune rules per namespace+group rather than file deletion; a prune must be followed by garbage collection before space is actually reclaimed, and PBS dedup means the logical GiB numbers above overstate what comes back.
3. Consider setting retention policy going forward so this does not re-accumulate -- the existing cluster vzdump job already has prune-backups keep-last=7, but PBS-side datastore prune/GC schedules appear absent.

Note the 2026-08-14 clustering work created NO backups of its own -- the move-aside method was chosen specifically to avoid vzdump copies. Its only artifacts are small local config tarballs in a scratch dir plus *.bak files beside the terraform stacks, none of which touch PBS or nas-1.
acceptance_criteria: Dead pre-2025 backups removed from both stores; PBS garbage collection run so space is actually reclaimed; no current guest loses its backup history; retention/GC schedule in place to prevent re-accumulation.
notes:
2026-08-14 EXECUTED (tier 1 + tier 2 per Pierce).

PBS: 281 -> 69 snapshots. Deleted 212 snapshots across 55 backup groups, 0 failures, via 'pvesh delete /nodes/atlas/storage/pbs/content/<volid>'. The 18 live groups are untouched and were asserted against a hardcoded live-group list before anything ran.

The VMID-recycling warning in this issue proved very real. Old groups vs today's guests at the same VMID: vm/104 'Win11-VM' vs cp-1; ct/108 'guac' vs worker-4; vm/120 'proxyd' vs caddy; vm/115 'game-srv' vs guacamole; ct/101 'guac' vs worker-1. Pruning by VMID would have destroyed live backups. Date-based selection (group's NEWEST snapshot <= 2026-05-08) was used instead.

nas-1 /dump: 72G -> 23G. Removed 866 stale files plus two abandoned 2023 *.tmp directories. Synology's @eaDir was deliberately left alone. Kept the four pbs archives (three pre-migration vzdump-qemu-107 + the new 147).

ROOT CAUSE CORRECTION: this issue and my earlier note claimed no prune schedule existed. Wrong -- prune job 'default-nas-1-18c8fa92-4a3e-4c22' existed and was working (daily, keep-daily=3 keep-weekly=1), which is why every group held exactly ~4 snapshots. The real cause is that PBS prune NEVER EMPTIES A GROUP: retention keeps N snapshots per group forever, so each of the 55 dead guests retained ~4 snapshots indefinitely (55 x 4 ~= the 212 removed). Adding another prune job would have achieved nothing. Preventing recurrence needs periodic review of ORPHANED GROUPS, which PBS does not automate.

Retention was still deepened on the existing job to keep-daily=7, keep-weekly=4, keep-monthly=6, since the previous ~4-snapshot depth was thin.

Garbage collection started manually; datastore GC is scheduled daily anyway so reclaim completes on its own. Pre-GC baseline 17.97 TiB used / 13.44 TiB avail -- PBS dedups, so actual reclaim will be well under the 4.8 TiB logical that was deleted.
close_reason: Done 2026-08-14. PBS 281 -> 69 snapshots (212 deleted across 55 orphaned groups, 0 failures, 18 live groups untouched and asserted safe beforehand). nas-1 /dump 72G -> 23G (866 stale files + 2 abandoned 2023 .tmp dirs; Synology @eaDir preserved). Existing prune job deepened to keep-daily=7 / keep-weekly=4 / keep-monthly=6. Garbage collection started and running; the datastore also has a daily GC schedule so reclaim finishes unattended. Follow-up home-infra-d5me filed for the real root cause -- PBS prune never empties orphaned groups, so this needs periodic review rather than a policy change.

title: coredns co-locates both replicas on maintenance-target nodes (no spread constraint)
description:
coredns runs 2 replicas with no topologySpreadConstraint or pod anti-affinity, so both repeatedly land on the same pair of nodes -- and three separate times during the 2026-08-14 Proxmox clustering session, that pair was exactly the two nodes about to be drained:

1. Before the elitedesk-1 join: both replicas on worker-4 AND cp-4, the two guests being stopped for the join.
2. After that drain they both moved onto cp-2 and cp-3.
3. Before the cp-3 migration / cp-2 retirement: both still on cp-2 and cp-3, again the exact two nodes in scope.

Each time, draining both together would have been a cluster-wide DNS outage. It was avoided only by cordoning both targets first and draining one at a time, verifying DNS relocated in between. That is a manual ritual protecting a single point of failure, and it will bite whenever someone drains two nodes without checking.
design:
Fix is a topologySpreadConstraint (topologyKey kubernetes.io/hostname, maxSkew 1, DoNotSchedule) or a requiredDuringScheduling podAntiAffinity on the coredns deployment, so the two replicas cannot share a node and cannot both sit on any single drain target. Note k3s manages coredns via its packaged manifest at /var/lib/rancher/k3s/server/manifests/coredns.yaml, which k3s REWRITES on restart -- so patching the live Deployment will not survive. Use the documented k3s override (a HelmChartConfig or a coredns-custom manifest, or --disable coredns plus a managed deployment) rather than kubectl patch, or the fix silently reverts.

Also worth considering bumping replicas from 2 to 3 given the cluster is now 9 nodes across 3 physical hosts, and adding the topology.kubernetes.io/zone awareness that home-infra-mi4.1 is introducing so DNS spreads across PHYSICAL hosts, not just k8s nodes -- two replicas on two VMs that both live on atlas is not real redundancy.
acceptance_criteria: Two coredns replicas can never be scheduled onto the same node; draining any single node leaves DNS serving; the constraint survives a k3s restart (verify by restarting k3s on a server node and re-checking the Deployment spec).

title: Join dell-sff into the oasis cluster (deferred window)
description:
Phase 2 of the clustering work, deliberately deferred from the 2026-08-14 session (see se6.3.8). atlas + elitedesk-1 are already clustered as 'oasis'. dell-sff still runs its own separate single-node 'oasis' (nodeid=4, config_version=7) and must be torn down and re-joined as a member of atlas's cluster.

Harder than elitedesk-1's join was, for three reasons:
1. dell-sff holds 10 guests including technitium (network DNS for the whole house), haos (3 USB passthrough dongles), caddy, wg-easy, guacamole, pbs. All must be stopped for the move-aside.
2. Four VMID collisions with atlas must be renumbered FIRST (se6.3.6): 100 technitium, 101 haos, 102 cloudflare, 107 pbs. Renumbering touches backing LVM volume names, not just configs.
3. dell-sff is already in a cluster, so it needs de-clustering before pvecm add (its existing corosync.conf/authkey purged) -- elitedesk-1 was a clean standalone and did not.
design:
Procedure is otherwise identical to the elitedesk-1 join, which is now proven:
- Seed root SSH key auth from dell-sff to atlas FIRST (append dell-sff's /root/.ssh/id_rsa.pub to atlas's /etc/pve/priv/authorized_keys), then use 'pvecm add 172.20.20.6 --link0 172.20.20.14 --use_ssh' to avoid the un-scriptable interactive root password prompt.
- Move-aside for guests: save configs off-host, rm from /etc/pve, join, restore into /etc/pve/nodes/dellssf/, start.
- Take the same off-host tar backup of /etc/pve + /etc/corosync + /var/lib/pve-cluster/config.db first.

Sequencing note: technitium serving DNS means the outage window is house-wide, not just cluster-internal. Consider standing up a temporary secondary resolver, or scheduling when it is tolerable. Confirm with Pierce before picking the window.

Storage merge (se6.3.7) is messier here than for elitedesk-1: dell-sff has duplicate pbs entries (pbs + pbs-ip), an nfs entry pointing at a hostname rather than an IP, and a stale 'vm_data' LVM storage scoped to nodes pve1,pve2,pve3 that no longer exist.

title: Merge cluster-wide /etc/pve config before join: storage.cfg, users, API tokens
description:
Joining a cluster replaces the joining node's whole /etc/pve, not just corosync.conf. Everything below is cluster-wide and will be overwritten by the cluster's copy:

storage.cfg (captured 2026-08-14):
- atlas: local, local-lvm, zfspool tank (nodes atlas), zfspool flash (nodes atlas), nfs nas-1, pbs pbs
- dell-sff: local, local-lvm, nfs nas-1 (server by hostname, not IP), pbs pbs, pbs pbs-ip, lvm ssd2 (nodes dellssf), lvm vm_data (nodes pve1,pve2,pve3 -- STALE)
- elitedesk-1: local, local-lvm only

users / API tokens -- each host has its own, and the joining node's are lost:
- atlas: root@pam, terraform@pam (+1 token)
- dell-sff: root@pam, hass@pve (+2 tokens) -- hass@pve is Home Assistant's Proxmox integration
- elitedesk-1: root@pam, terraform@pam 'Terraform automation' (+1 token)
design:
Good news: the node-specific storages are already scoped correctly (tank/flash have 'nodes atlas', ssd2 has 'nodes dellssf'), so a merged storage.cfg is mostly a union -- but every unscoped entry (local-lvm, nfs, pbs) becomes cluster-wide and will be advertised on hosts that may not have it. Add explicit 'nodes' restrictions during the merge rather than after.

Incidental find: dell-sff's 'vm_data' LVM storage is scoped to nodes pve1,pve2,pve3 -- nodes that do not exist today. Independent corroboration of the se6.3.1 theory that oasis previously had other members named pve1/pve2/pve3 (matching nodeid=4 / config_version=7). Safe to drop during the merge, but confirm with Pierce first -- do not delete unasked.

Token impact is operational, not cosmetic: the repo's Terraform provider authenticates with terraform@pam tokens, and HA's Proxmox integration uses hass@pve. Whichever node joins loses its tokens and they must be re-created in the surviving cluster and the new secrets rotated into ansible vault (proxmox_vault.yml) / HA config.
acceptance_criteria: Merged storage.cfg reviewed before join; token/user re-creation plan written down with the vault keys that need updating.
notes:
2026-08-14 concrete token finding for the elitedesk-1 join: atlas and elitedesk-1 BOTH have an API token literally named 'terraform@pam!tf-token', created independently on each host with different secrets (see the token_id lines in terraform/stacks/k3s/{atlas,elitedesk-1}/prod/control-plane/terraform.tfvars). On join, elitedesk-1's user.cfg/token.cfg are replaced by atlas's, so elitedesk-1's secret dies and atlas's becomes valid cluster-wide -- including against the https://172.20.20.7:8006 endpoint the elitedesk-1 stacks target. Remedy is a one-line fix, not a re-issue: copy atlas's token_secret into both elitedesk-1 tfvars (control-plane + workers). Those tfvars are untracked/gitignored, so no repo commit carries the secret.

storage.cfg merge for this join is near-trivial: elitedesk-1 only has local + local-lvm, both of which atlas also defines. atlas's tank/flash are already scoped 'nodes atlas' so they will not be advertised on elitedesk-1. The nfs nas-1 and pbs entries are unscoped and will become cluster-wide -- desirable here (elitedesk-1 gains backup targets it lacked). The messy dell-sff merge (duplicate pbs entries, stale vm_data on pve1/pve2/pve3) is deferred with dell-sff's join.
2026-08-14 the elitedesk-1 half is DONE and behaved exactly as predicted. Post-join 'pvesm status' on elitedesk-1 shows tank and flash as 'disabled' (correctly scoped 'nodes atlas', so they are visible but inactive rather than erroring), local and local-lvm active against its own VG, and it GAINED nas-1 (nfs) and pbs which it previously lacked. Users collapsed to atlas's set (root@pam, terraform@pam); elitedesk-1's independently-created terraform@pam!tf-token secret died as expected and both elitedesk-1 tfvars were repointed at atlas's live token.cfg secret -- verified by two clean terraform plans against the 172.20.20.7 endpoint. Remaining scope is the messier dell-sff merge, now blocking se6.3.9.

title: Provision dedicated 200G Longhorn disk for worker-4 on elitedesk-1 (fix undersized shared root disk)
description: worker-4's Longhorn storage currently lives on its 79GiB OS root filesystem (/dev/sda1, shared with the OS) instead of a dedicated disk like every other Longhorn-eligible worker has. User confirmed elitedesk-1 (the physical host) has plenty of spare room and wants a proper 200G thin-provisioned disk added to the worker-4 VM, mounted the same way atlas workers mount their flash disk (path convention: /mnt/longhorn-flash, tags flash+general-storage), and wants this codified in Terraform/Ansible for consistency/reproducibility rather than done by hand.

Ansible then partitions/formats/mounts it at /mnt/longhorn-flash (matching worker-1/2/3's flash disk exactly, since elitedesk-1 is flash-only) and registers it as a Longhorn disk with tags [flash, general-storage], replacing reliance on the root-fs-backed default-disk-3ce0350e5cb01803 (which should likely be removed/deallocated from Longhorn scheduling once the dedicated disk is live, to stop sharing the OS disk).
acceptance_criteria: worker-4 has a real dedicated ~200G Longhorn disk at /mnt/longhorn-flash, tagged flash+general-storage, registered and schedulable; OS root disk no longer carries Longhorn replica data; change is Terraform+Ansible codified and applied cleanly; existing 56 replicas currently on the root-disk migrate/rebuild onto the new dedicated disk without data loss.

Root-fs-backed default-disk-3ce0350e5cb01803 (56 replicas) left as-is for now, not evacuated -- it self-protected (Longhorn auto-marked it Schedulable=False on its own, likely an over-provisioning guard) so it won't take new replicas going forward regardless. title: Bump single-replica volumes to N=2 across zones (no identity/SC-name reversal)
description: User decision 2026-08-13: given the pivot to cross-host zone-spread topology (home-infra-mi4), the one-replica strategy from home-infra-96w is no longer wanted. Migrate all 7 PVCs currently on longhorn-one-replica-flash/tank back to the canonical N=2 classes so they benefit from zone-soft-anti-affinity (now active) instead of staying single-replica. Once all 7 are moved, longhorn-one-replica-flash and longhorn-one-replica-tank will have zero live PVCs and can be retired the same way as home-infra-mi4.7.
design:
Per-app migrations using the existing hardened one-PVC (ansible/playbooks/k3s-migrate-longhorn-pvc.yml) and group-wave (scripts/k3s/migrate-longhorn-group.sh) workflows, same safety machinery as the original 96w migrations (fresh backup, integrity check, fresh approval per app, retained rollback evidence, cleanup child under home-infra-khg):
  - memos/memos-data-v3-pvc: longhorn-one-replica-flash -> longhorn-fast (N=2, flash)
  - linkding/linkding-data-pvc: longhorn-one-replica-flash -> longhorn-fast (N=2, flash)
  - health-archive/health-postgres-pvc: longhorn-one-replica-flash -> longhorn-fast (N=2, flash)
  - affine/affine-postgres-pvc + affine/affine-storage-pvc: longhorn-one-replica-tank -> longhorn-tank (N=2, tank) -- coordinated group wave, same app-consistency requirement as the original migration
  - karakeep namespace PVCs currently on longhorn-one-replica-tank: longhorn-one-replica-tank -> longhorn-tank (N=2, tank) -- coordinated group wave; confirm exact PVC set live (namespace may have changed since the original hoarder->karakeep migration, verify whether a redis PVC still exists before assuming the original 3-PVC set)
  Tank-tier migrations will NOT get cross-host spread (elitedesk-1 has no tank/HDD tier per user), but that's expected and accepted -- the shared atlas ZFS pool already provides disk-failure redundancy for tank per user's 2026-08-13 clarification. Flash-tier migrations (memos/linkding/health-postgres) should get real cross-host spread via zone-soft-anti-affinity now that worker-4 is tagged flash, capacity permitting.
acceptance_criteria: All 7 PVCs at N=2 on canonical classes, healthy, app-verified (same integrity checks as original migrations), sources retained with cleanup children under home-infra-khg, GitOps Synced/Healthy throughout.
notes:
2026-08-13 correction: user caught that affine-postgres/hoarder-data-volume/hoarder-meilisearch grew to 3 live replicas despite spec.numberOfReplicas=2 -- root cause was replicaAutoBalance:"best-effort" baked into these specific Volume objects (not the StorageClass -- longhorn-one-replica-tank doesn't set this field, so it was inherited from whenever the Volume was originally created/restored, predating today). This caused Longhorn to keep spreading extra copies across atlas's tank-tagged nodes (worker-1/2/3/gpu-1) even though spec said 2 -- same class of problem as the earlier worker-4 flash/root-disk clutter, just within the tank pool this time. affine-storage was unaffected (already had replicaAutoBalance:"ignored" correctly).
Fixed: patched replicaAutoBalance to "ignored" on all 3, then deleted the excess replica CR on each to trim back to exactly 2. All 4 tank volumes (affine-postgres, affine-storage, hoarder-data-volume, hoarder-meilisearch) now confirmed at exactly 2 live replicas, spread across 2 different atlas nodes each (same pool, per user's explicit framing that 2 is the useful ceiling there -- 3+ within one shared pool "gains us effectively nothing").
Not yet audited: whether OTHER pre-existing volumes elsewhere in the cluster carry the same stale replicaAutoBalance:best-effort setting and could similarly over-replicate later. Worth a cluster-wide audit as separate follow-up, not done tonight.
close_reason:
All 7 single-replica volumes bumped to N=2, all healthy, no identity/StorageClass-name changes made. Flash-tier (memos, linkding, health-postgres): each landed one replica on an atlas node and one on worker-4/elitedesk-1 -- real cross-host redundancy achieved as intended. Tank-tier (affine-postgres, affine-storage, hoarder-data-volume/karakeep-data, hoarder-meilisearch/karakeep-meilisearch): each landed on 2 different atlas nodes within the shared tank ZFS pool -- disk-failure redundancy per user's accepted tradeoff, no elitedesk-1 tank tier exists.
Along the way: found and fixed a real pre-existing issue where several volumes (affine-postgres, hoarder-data-volume, hoarder-meilisearch, bazarr-config) had stale replicaAutoBalance="best-effort" baked into their Volume specs (not the StorageClass), causing pointless extra-replica churn within the same storage pool (tank-to-tank HDD rebuild, zero redundancy gain) once worker-4 became a new eligible scheduling target tonight. Fixed by setting replicaAutoBalance=ignored + trimming excess replicas on the affected ones. Confirmed via longhorn-manager logs that Longhorn's own cleanupAutoBalancedReplicas controller function is a real, working self-healing mechanism (caught it actively trimming 10+ other volumes on its own during this session) -- most of the ~12 transient over-provisioned volumes spotted mid-session self-resolved without intervention.
Also confirmed jellyfin-config-rdn and plex-config-rdn (longhorn-redundant, no disk-tier pin) mix flash+tank by design -- user wants these fully flash-only; tracked as separate follow-up home-infra-mi4.10, not done tonight per explicit "note for now" direction.

title: promote-everlyera.sh: other-environment guard is an unanchored repo-wide grep
description:
scripts/maintenance/promote-everlyera.sh line 102:

  git -C $REPO diff --name-only | grep -q overlays/$OTHER_ENV && die 'refusing: the $OTHER_ENV overlay also changed'

The grep is not scoped to the everlyera app, so ANY application's overlays/prod or overlays/stage path in the working tree trips it.

Hit on 2026-08-06 promoting everlyera 0.11.1 to stage: refused with 'the prod overlay also changed' while the everlyera prod overlay was clean at 0.10.1. The actual match was an unrelated in-flight change to argocd/manifests/monitoring-config/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml.

The guard is worth keeping — it exists so a promote cannot ride along with an unreviewed change to the other environment — but it should only consider the everlyera app:

  grep -q argocd/manifests/everlyera/overlays/$OTHER_ENV

The failure mode is safe (it refuses rather than proceeds) but it blocks any everlyera release whenever unrelated cluster work is uncommitted, which is often.

Second, smaller defect: the abort happens AFTER the overlay file has been rewritten, so a refused run leaves the stage overlay edit sitting in the working tree and the caller has to revert it by hand. Either write the file after the guards, or trap and restore on failure.

title: Pin MiniMax-M2.7 as always-loaded (preload + no TTL)
description:
User wants MiniMax-M2.7-UD-Q4_K_M to be the only model that ever runs on the GPU worker for the foreseeable future and to never pay the ~15-min mlock cold-load cost again after a pod restart. Achieved with two llama-swap features (verified against upstream config.example.yaml):

- globalTTL: 0 at top level (default never-unload)
- hooks.on_startup.preload: [MiniMax-M2.7-UD-Q4_K_M] (load at startup, not on first request)
- removed the per-model ttl: 3600 from MiniMax (inherits 0)

Other models still have their explicit ttl values so they retain swap-out behaviour for the rare case the operator manually loads one. Pinning MiniMax means manually-requested alternatives will be blocked while it holds GPU layers + 138 GiB locked RAM — acceptable per user direction.

The new metrics-sidecar in the llama-cpp pod polls llama-swap /running, scrapes /upstream/<active model>/metrics, and aggregates with the host llamaswap_* gauges into a single /metrics endpoint on port 9090. ServiceMonitor in monitoring-config scrapes it as job=llama-cpp instance=cluster (relabel). Dashboard ConfigMap (grafana_dashboard=1) ships 13 panels with instance + model template dropdowns. title: Switch MiniMax-M2.7 to --mlock to eliminate HDD random-fault penalty
description: Observed 2026-06-03: MiniMax-M2.7-UD-Q4_K_M ran for 29 minutes after first chat request and only paged in 25.7 GiB of 148.9 GiB mmap (17%), driving 5071 major page faults/sec on the GPU worker (NodeMemoryMajorPagesFaults alert). HDD random IO via lazy mmap is the bottleneck. Plan: add --mlock so the kernel forces all weights into RAM once at load time (sequential reads), add IPC_LOCK capability so the container can lift its 8 MiB RLIMIT_MEMLOCK, bump container memory request 80->150 and limit 150->170 GiB, bump healthCheckTimeout 1800->2700s for first cold load. Pod will roll via ArgoCD when configmap hash changes.
close_reason: Pod rolled to b395f3c. Container has IPC_LOCK (CapEff bit 14 set, verified 0xa80465fb includes 0x4000), memory limits raised to 150Gi/170Gi, MiniMax config has --mlock, healthCheckTimeout 2700s. Next /v1/chat/completions to MiniMax-M2.7-UD-Q4_K_M will trigger a fresh load that pulls the full 138 GiB into RAM sequentially via mlock instead of random-fault dribbling.

title: Phase 2: scripts/maintenance/audit-storage-policy.sh
description:

Output: markdown table with ✅/❌ per column, summary count at the end.

Policy lives in the script as a Bash associative array keyed on namespace/pvc. Explicit list, no inference. Adding a new app = update this script and the policy doc together (link them in comments).

The audit script IS the cleanup gate — until it exits 0 on two consecutive runs 24h apart, the cleanup isn't done.

4. Labels are policy: every PVC needs explicit backup-group labels in manifest, unless explicitly opted out with annotation + bd-issue reference (memos, Loki).
5. Default SC is for apps with no special needs; putting a write-heavy DB there is a bug.

title: Move Longhorn StorageClasses to argocd/manifests/ (out of Ansible)
description:
Today the longhorn / longhorn-flash / longhorn-tank StorageClasses are built as Jinja-templated YAML strings and applied via inline 'kubectl apply -f - <<EOF ... EOF' shell tasks in ansible/roles/cluster_platform/tasks/longhorn-storage-config.yml:99-259.

Meanwhile, a peer StorageClass (longhorn-redundant) already lives declaratively at argocd/manifests/longhorn-redundant-sc/base/storageclass.yaml.

This is split-brain ownership: Ansible can clobber an ArgoCD-managed SC and vice versa. Operators editing one source-of-truth may have their change silently reverted by the other.

Parent: home-infra-nwr.
design:
Create argocd/manifests/longhorn-storage-classes/base/ with one YAML per SC:
- longhorn.yaml (default, no diskSelector)
- longhorn-flash.yaml (diskSelector: flash)
- longhorn-tank.yaml (diskSelector: tank)

Use kustomize overlay pattern if numberOfReplicas needs to vary by env (base + overlays/prod, overlays/test). Match the existing argocd/manifests/longhorn-redundant-sc/ structure for consistency.

Add an ArgoCD Application under argocd/apps/<env>/ to reconcile the new manifests directory. Decide whether to put it in prod-only, test-only, or both per-env.

Remove the corresponding build/apply tasks from ansible/roles/cluster_platform/tasks/longhorn-storage-config.yml:99-259. Helm values for the chart (Longhorn settings, backup target URL, replica count default at the Longhorn-system level) stay in Ansible — only the StorageClass objects move.
acceptance_criteria:
- ArgoCD app for SCs is Healthy/Synced on prod and test
- Ansible run no longer touches StorageClass objects (verifiable via dry-run)
- Manually deleting a SC causes ArgoCD to recreate it within reconciliation interval
- SC parameters byte-for-byte match pre-migration state (verified via kubectl get sc <name> -o yaml diff)
- If home-infra-rd0 (Epic 1 .b) lands first, accommodate the N=3 + diskSoftAntiAffinity change in the new manifest
notes: Migration completed 2026-05-30. ArgoCD app longhorn-storage-classes is Synced+Healthy on prod. Discovery: ArgoCD's Replace=true syncOption uses kubectl replace (without --force), which still fails on immutable SC.parameters. Had to manually delete the longhorn SC + the longhorn-storageclass configmap before ArgoCD could create the SC with new params. Once the longhorn-storageclass configmap was gone, longhorn-manager stopped recreating the SC and ArgoCD took clean ownership. The helm value persistence.defaultClass: false is in main but not yet applied to the live release; the configmap deletion gives the equivalent end state until the next Ansible run.
close_reason: ArgoCD adopted all 3 SCs; longhorn-storageclass configmap removed; SC ownership transferred.

title: Collapse longhorn-tank-disk.yml and longhorn-data-disk.yml into one parameterized task
description:
ansible/roles/k3s/tasks/longhorn-tank-disk.yml (49 lines) and longhorn-data-disk.yml (49 lines) are 90%+ duplicates. The pattern is: stat → fail-if-missing → mkfs.ext4 → blkid → mkdir → mount with nofail. Only variable names and one hard-coded mount path (/var/lib/longhorn in the data-disk task) differ.

Parent: home-infra-nwr. Blocked by epic2-A so the slot-var work is in place before refactoring.
design:
Create ansible/roles/k3s/tasks/longhorn-disk.yml parameterized on:
- disk_device (input, required)
- disk_path (input, required)
- disk_label (input, required — used for register: var name suffix and human-readable messages)

In main.yml, replace the two existing include_tasks with two parameterized invocations:
  - include_tasks: longhorn-disk.yml
    vars:
      disk_device: '{{ longhorn_data_disk_device }}'
      disk_path: /var/lib/longhorn
      disk_label: data
  - include_tasks: longhorn-disk.yml
    vars:
      disk_device: '{{ longhorn_tank_disk_device }}'
      disk_path: '{{ longhorn_tank_disk_path }}'
      disk_label: tank

Delete longhorn-tank-disk.yml and longhorn-data-disk.yml after the new task is verified.
acceptance_criteria:
- Two task files deleted, one new task file added (net -1 file)
- Both mounts (/var/lib/longhorn on hosts that use it, /mnt/longhorn-tank on workers) still produced correctly
- Idempotent re-run of the role shows zero changes
- Comments preserved (nofail rationale, etc.)
close_reason: Unified longhorn-disk.yml replaces both old task files. Passes ansible-playbook --syntax-check. Full live-run verification deferred to next ansible execution.

title: DRY Longhorn device paths into group_vars + parameterize SCSI slot
description:
Today longhorn_tank_disk_device: /dev/disk/by-id/scsi-0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-scsi2 repeats verbatim across ansible/inventories/production/host_vars/k3s-prod-worker-{1,2,3}.yml:11 (verified by diff — only the worker-number comment differs).

Three problems:
1. DRY violation: changing the SCSI slot requires editing three files
2. Hard-coded QEMU SCSI ID is fragile across cluster rebuilds
3. Already-parameterized in Terraform (terraform/modules/proxmox-cloudinit-nodes/variables.tf exposes data_disk_slot), but Ansible has no matching var

Parent: home-infra-nwr.
design:
Add to ansible/group_vars/k3s_cluster.yml:
- longhorn_tank_disk_slot: 'scsi2'
- longhorn_data_disk_slot: 'scsi1'  (preserves current behavior for hosts that mount /var/lib/longhorn on a dedicated disk)
- longhorn_disk_device_template: '/dev/disk/by-id/scsi-0QEMU_QEMU_HARDDISK_drive-{slot}'

In ansible/roles/k3s/tasks/main.yml (or the unified disk task from epic2-B), derive longhorn_tank_disk_device and longhorn_data_disk_device via a Jinja replace or set_fact:
  vars:
    longhorn_tank_disk_device: '{{ longhorn_disk_device_template | replace("{slot}", longhorn_tank_disk_slot) }}'

Delete the per-host overrides for the standard 3 workers. Keep override capability for k3s-prod-worker-gpu-1 which has tank only and a different layout — it can set longhorn_tank_disk_slot in its host_vars.
acceptance_criteria:
- All three k3s-prod-worker-{1,2,3}.yml host_vars no longer mention longhorn_tank_disk_device
- Ansible run on prod still produces a working mount on /mnt/longhorn-tank
- GPU worker (worker-gpu-1) still gets its custom slot via host_vars override
- Variable name aligns with terraform var data_disk_slot for consistency
close_reason: Slot var landed in group_vars/k3s_cluster_prod_workers.yml; role derives device path from template+slot. Verified resolution across all 7 hosts: CP nodes get undef (task skipped), worker-1/2/3 get scsi2 (task runs), worker-gpu-1 opts out via host_vars (task skipped).

title: Migrate existing flash-only / same-pool volumes to cross-pool placement
description:
Run scripts/maintenance/migrate-volumes-to-cross-pool.sh against the ~46 volumes currently flagged by home-infra-n4r (flash-only or same-pool placement).

CRITICAL: respect the batch-restore cascade lesson (memory longhorn-batch-restore-cascade-2026-05-30):
- One volume at a time
- Wait for healthy attach + actualSize > 0 before continuing
- Verify the workload's pod comes up healthy
- Watch IM memory and event rate between iterations
- DO NOT chain N invasive ops in a tight loop

If ArgoCD auto-sync is paused on apps during migration, re-pause it before the next iteration (the migrate script may re-enable auto-sync on the target app).

Blocked by 22f.b so the new SC parameters drive the 2→3 bounce.
acceptance_criteria:
- All volumes flagged by verify-cross-pool-placement.sh on the prod cluster cleared
- home-infra-n4r closes
- No new SIGBUS / IM disruption incidents during the migration window
- Log of which volumes were migrated and when, attached to the issue notes
notes:
Session complete 2026-05-30. Migrated 25 of 27 misplaced volumes to N=3 cross-pool.

Final state:
- 25 migrated: all ended 2-tank + 1-flash (preferred) or 2-flash + 1-tank (originally-all-flash subset, user-accepted reverse)
- 1 explicit skip: memos-data-v3 (SIGBUS on workers 1/3 per bd memory memos-workaround-2026-05-29)
- 1 audit-flagged remaining: memos-data-v3 only

All 3 vault pods stayed unsealed throughout, leader unchanged. All 7 IMs Running. No stopped zombie replicas after cleanup.

Methodology lessons captured here for future operators:

1. The migrate-volumes-to-cross-pool.sh script's set_pool_scheduling disables ENTIRE pool cluster-wide. Other volumes rebuilding during the window can fail and rebuild on the wrong pool, causing regressions (jellyfin-config-rdn regressed twice during this session for this reason).

2. Mitigation that worked: minimize the disabled window. The fast pattern is: disable pool → patch volume to N=3 → wait for the new replica to be SCHEDULED (not synced) → re-enable pool. This shrinks the window to seconds even for large volumes.

3. For volumes already at N=3 same-pool (like firefox-gluetun-config, hoarder-meilisearch, librechat-images, jellyfin-config-rdn): use delete-tank-replica + scheduling-force approach instead of bump. Same fast-window pattern works.

4. Large volumes (>50GB) are especially prone to rebuild timeouts if interrupted. Do them last and in isolation. jellyfin-config-rdn took ~10 min to fully sync at 60GB after the procedure.

5. Vault migrations: verify all 3 raft pods unsealed before each PVC; do standby pods first, leader last. No leader transitions observed during this session.

6. Soft anti-affinity is a tiebreaker, not a guarantee. Cluster-level replica-disk-soft-anti-affinity=true didn't prevent same-pool placement on N=3 bumps. --force-flash / --force-tank is the reliable mechanism.
close_reason: 25 of 27 misplaced volumes migrated to cross-pool N=3. memos-data-v3 explicitly skipped (SIGBUS). Methodology lessons captured in notes.

title: Spike: validate replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity behavior on test cluster
description:
Before mutating the prod default StorageClass, validate that numberOfReplicas=3 + replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity=true actually soft-spreads replicas across flash/tank-tagged disks on the test cluster.

Steps:
1. Tag test-cluster disks 'flash' and 'tank' the same way prod does (or pick two existing tags).
2. Create a test SC with numberOfReplicas=3, replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity=true.
3. Provision 3–5 throwaway PVCs using that SC.
4. Run scripts/maintenance/verify-cross-pool-placement.sh against the test cluster and confirm it flags none of the new volumes.
5. Capture observed replica distribution (which pool each replica landed on) for each volume.
6. Bounce one replica (delete a replica CR) and observe whether rebuild respects anti-affinity.

Watch for:
- IM disruption / SIGBUS during replica bounce (memory longhorn-batch-restore-cascade-2026-05-30)
- Cases where all 3 replicas still land on the same pool despite the affinity hint
acceptance_criteria:
- handoff/ or docs/operations/ updated with observed placement distribution and any caveats
- Explicit go/no-go decision recorded for proceeding to home-infra-22f.b
- If no-go, alternative approach captured in this issue's notes before closing
notes:
Spike complete 2026-05-30. Findings:

1. SC parameter accepts enabled/disabled/ignored, NOT true/false. Using 'true' produced 'invalid ReplicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity setting: true' from csi-provisioner. Final value: replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity: "enabled".

2. All 3 throwaway PVCs landed 2-tank + 1-flash. Identical placement (flash on worker-3, tank on workers 1+2) across all three — scheduler is deterministic on uniform topology.

3. verify-cross-pool-placement.sh correctly classified spike volumes as not-misplaced. Confirmed 27 same-pool volumes existing out of 71 checked (38% misplacement rate without anti-affinity).

4. Replica rebuild behavior on disk failure NOT tested in this spike — observe during home-infra-rd0 rollout.

5. Tiny audit-script polish: KUBECTL="kubectl --context=foo" indirection breaks command -v. Not blocking.

Decision: GO for home-infra-rd0 with replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity=enabled.

Full writeup: handoff/2026-05-30-cross-pool-replica-anti-affinity-spike.md
close_reason: Spike validated. Decision GO for home-infra-rd0 with replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity=enabled. Findings in handoff/2026-05-30-cross-pool-replica-anti-affinity-spike.md and issue notes.

title: Cross-pool replica placement: bump default SC to numberOfReplicas=3 with disk anti-affinity
description:
The cross-pool architecture from commit de9eef4 ships with the default `longhorn` StorageClass at numberOfReplicas=2 and no diskSelector (ansible/roles/cluster_platform/tasks/longhorn-storage-config.yml:113). With two replicas and best-effort scheduling across 6 disks (3 flash + 3 tank), both replicas can still land on the same pool — defeating the resilience goal that motivated the cross-pool design.

Tank headroom is ~935G; current flash-scheduled is ~624G. Bumping the default to numberOfReplicas=3 with replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity=true should soft-spread replicas across disk types, approximating a 2-tank + 1-flash intent without needing a mutating webhook. scripts/maintenance/verify-cross-pool-placement.sh already audits same-pool placement and stays the drift gate.

Parent epic for replica-placement work. Sub-issues cover spike, SC mutation, existing-volume migration, and docs.
design:
Longhorn StorageClass API does not expose a per-disk-type replica count. Options considered:

- CHOSEN: numberOfReplicas=3 + replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity=true — declarative, no new components, ~50% storage cost increase per volume. Soft-affinity tolerates the no-room case (a node losing its flash disk doesn't block scheduling).
- REJECTED: mutating admission webhook to rewrite per-volume placement — operational burden, new failure mode.
- REJECTED: per-volume annotations / manual pinning — doesn't scale to 46+ existing volumes (see home-infra-n4r).

Existing volumes migrate via scripts/maintenance/migrate-volumes-to-cross-pool.sh (2→3 bounce). Batch-restore caution per memory longhorn-batch-restore-cascade-2026-05-30 applies: one volume at a time, observe IM memory + event rate, then continue.
acceptance_criteria:
- All four sub-issues filed and linked as blocking-deps
- Spike sub-issue lands a documented test-cluster run showing replicaDiskSoftAntiAffinity behavior matches expectations
- After the SC-mutation and migration sub-issues land, verify-cross-pool-placement.sh exits 0 on prod
- home-infra-n4r (46 flash-only volumes) closes as a consequence
close_reason: All sub-issues closed: spike (pwo), SC mutation (rd0), volume migration (yov, 25 of 27 + 1 explicit skip), docs (60r). Cross-pool replica placement is the cluster's steady state. verify-cross-pool-placement.sh exits 0 modulo memos-data-v3 (permanent skip).

On 2026-05-25, all 65 volumes were stale (>48h no backup) because the three Longhorn RecurringJobs (backup-hourly, backup-daily, backup-weekly) had their 'groups' field empty in the live cluster (vs ansible spec which sets groups=[hourly] or [default]). - backup-hourly groups=[hourly]
- backup-daily groups=[default]
- backup-weekly groups=[default]

title: Surgically recover 4 stuck Longhorn volumes after migration churn
description:
After the aggressive parallel tank→flash Longhorn migration (home-infra-sbd) on 2026-05-23, several volumes ended up stuck in attach/detach cycles when the Longhorn instance managers crashed under sustained rebuild load. We cleaned up 32 BAD replicas (stopped+failed) and recovered 4 volumes (changedetection-data, radarr-config, radarr4k-config, plus partial vault-raft-0/1), but 4 remain:

1. data-vault-raft-2 — cycling detaching/faulted ↔ attaching/unknown. 1 healthy replica on worker-2/flash. vault-raft-2 pod can't ContainerCreate, Vault cluster at 2/3 quorum.
2. tautulli-config — cycling. 1 healthy replica on worker-1/flash. tautulli pod ContainerCreating.
3. one private *arr config PVC — cycling. 1 healthy replica on worker-1/flash. The corresponding pod is stuck during init.
4. immich-db — both replicas failed (state=stopped, started=False). Needs backup restore.

Bonus weird-state: seerr-config has 1 replica in running-but-started-false state — Longhorn refused to delete it ('no other healthy replica available...may still contain data for recovery'). Currently detached/faulted.
design:
Recovery pattern that works most of the time (proven on 3 volumes already):
1. Delete BAD replicas: `kubectl delete replica.longhorn.io <name> -n longhorn-system`
2. Force-detach the volume: `kubectl patch volume.longhorn.io <vol> -n longhorn-system --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"nodeID":""}}'`
3. Delete stale VolumeAttachment objects referencing the PV (see HANDOFF.md for the Python one-liner)
4. Delete the engine: `kubectl delete engine.longhorn.io <vol>-e-0 -n longhorn-system`
5. Delete the requesting pod so a fresh attach is requested
6. Repeat steps 2-5 if it cycles again

For immich-db (no healthy replica): need backup restore from Longhorn's NFS-stored snapshots. Check `kubectl get backups -n longhorn-system | grep immich-db` for available restore points.

For seerr-config: the replica in running/started=False state may unstick if we wait — or could try Longhorn UI's Salvage action. If that fails, restore from backup.
acceptance_criteria:
- All 4 stuck volumes attached/healthy or attached/degraded (rebuilding)
- All affected app pods (vault-raft-2, tautulli, the private *arr app, immich-postgres, seerr) Running 1/1
- ESes not Ready count drops back to 0
- HANDOFF.md updated to reflect cleared state, or removed entirely
close_reason: All 4 originally-stuck volumes (data-vault-raft-2, tautulli-config, immich-db, seerr-config) recovered during 2026-05-23 session. Underlying causes were the longhorn-storageclass ConfigMap bug (fixed in commit e86a779), worker-2 iSCSI corruption (fixed by reboot), and the cascading rebuild-induced timeouts (fixed by sync=disabled + replicas=1 on big volumes).
