title: Prometheus alert: Vault has no active leader for >5m
description:
The 2026-05-21 incident where the Vault Raft cluster sat in a no-leader state for >40 minutes was discovered only when ESO-dependent apps started failing to refresh secrets, not by an alert.

Vault exports a Prometheus metric `vault_core_active{}` (1 = active, 0 = standby/sealed). We should fire a critical alert when no pod has `vault_core_active == 1` for sustained time.

Bonus alerts to consider in the same rule group:
- vault_core_unsealed == 0 for >5m on any pod (leader-independent)
- vault_raft_replication_appendEntries_logs == 0 for >5m on standby pods (replication stalled)
design:
Vault is already scraped (it has a /sys/metrics?format=prometheus endpoint). Add a PrometheusRule under argocd/manifests/monitoring-config/.

Example rule:

  - alert: VaultClusterNoActiveLeader
    expr: max by () (vault_core_active) == 0
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: critical
    annotations:
      summary: "Vault cluster has no active leader"
      description: "No Vault pod reports vault_core_active=1 for the past 5 minutes — Raft is stuck. Likely cause: TLS cluster cert mismatch after pod IP/addr drift. See docs/recovery/vault-cluster-cert-recovery.md."

  - alert: VaultPodSealed
    expr: vault_core_unsealed == 0
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: warning

Route critical via the existing ntfy-prod-critical receiver in alertmanager.
acceptance_criteria:
- PrometheusRule added under argocd/manifests/monitoring-config/, applied, visible in `kubectl get prometheusrule -A`
- Synthetic test: scale vault-raft StatefulSet to 0, wait 6 minutes, alert fires through ntfy
- VaultPodSealed warning fires when a single pod is sealed (intentional or otherwise)

title: Auto-recover Vault no-leader / stale cluster-cert state in vault-unseal.yml
description:
On 2026-05-21 the Vault Raft cluster failed to elect a leader after a host reboot. Symptoms: all 3 pods unsealed and present in raft config, but inter-pod cluster RPC on port 8201 failed with `remote error: tls: unrecognized name`. Root cause was that the auto-generated cluster TLS cert (stored in encrypted Vault core data) had been issued against a `cluster_addr` value that no longer matched the pods' current `VAULT_CLUSTER_ADDR` env var. Only an active leader can regenerate that cert; no leader can be elected because the cert is broken. Chicken and egg.

Recovery required manual intervention:
1. Scale StatefulSet to 0
2. Spawn a temporary pod mounting all 3 vault PVCs
3. Wipe /vault/data on vault-raft-1 and vault-raft-2
4. Write a single-node peers.json on vault-raft-0 (only itself as voter)
5. Scale to 1, unseal vault-raft-0 → it bootstraps as a single-node cluster and elects itself leader, regenerating the cluster cert against current cluster_addr
6. Scale to 3; vault-raft-1 and vault-raft-2 boot empty, retry_join finds the leader, get a snapshot, unseal each → cluster healed

ansible/playbooks/maintenance/vault-unseal.yml currently does NOT detect this state. It tries to unseal followers, succeeds (sealed-state is unrelated), then fails at the "Login to Vault" task because the active service has no endpoints. The error is generic ("12 retries exhausted") and hides the underlying TLS issue.
design:
Add a new task block after "Assert all Vault pods are unsealed":

1. Poll for active leader: `kubectl exec ... vault status` and check `HA Mode=active`. Retry for ~60 seconds.
2. If no leader after polling AND pod logs show repeated `tls: unrecognized name` errors on port 8201, declare the cert-drift recovery condition.
3. Execute the documented recovery:
   - Scale StatefulSet to 0
   - Apply a recovery Pod manifest mounting all 3 data-vault-raft-N PVCs
   - Wipe vault-raft-1 and vault-raft-2 /vault/data
   - Write single-node peers.json on vault-raft-0 (selecting whichever node has the highest Raft index from the survey)
   - Scale to 1, wait for Running
   - Unseal vault-raft-0 with the keys from the vault-init secret
   - Wait for HA Mode=active
   - Scale to 3
   - Wait for vault-raft-1 and vault-raft-2 Running
   - Unseal each with the keys
   - Verify all 3 voters via `vault operator raft list-peers`
4. Make this opt-in via a tagged role (--tags vault-recover-cluster-cert) so the destructive recovery doesn't fire on a transient slow election.

Reference: docs/recovery/vault-cluster-cert-recovery.md (to be added) capturing the procedure prose for humans.
acceptance_criteria:
- Re-running vault-unseal.yml on a cluster in the cert-drift state automatically heals it without manual intervention.
- The playbook is idempotent — running it twice in a row with a healthy cluster is a no-op.
- A new runbook (docs/recovery/vault-cluster-cert-recovery.md) documents the procedure and the symptoms that trigger it.
- The argocd/apps/prod/vault.yaml uncommitted clusterAddr pin is committed as a complementary defense-in-depth fix.
notes:
2026-05-21 implementation committed in 7995103 + b79aef5:

1. argocd/apps/prod/vault.yaml — pinned server.ha.clusterAddr to "http://$(HOSTNAME).vault-raft-internal:8201" to prevent silent chart-template drift.

2. ansible/playbooks/maintenance/vault-unseal.yml — added detect+recover branch (~315 LOC inserted between "Assert all Vault pods are unsealed" and "Login to Vault"):
   - Waits up to ~90 s for a Raft leader on the primary pod
   - If no leader: greps recent logs for "tls: unrecognized name" cluster RPC errors
   - Default: fails with diagnostic message + exact re-run command
   - With -e vault_recover_cluster_cert=true: executes the documented recovery (scale to 0 → recovery pod mounts all PVCs → wipe followers → single-node peers.json on primary → scale to 1 + unseal + wait active → scale to full + unseal followers + verify list-peers)
   - Reuses existing vault_unseal_keys / vault_root_token facts; recovery branch is idempotent — re-running on a healthy cluster is a no-op

3. docs/recovery/vault-cluster-cert-recovery.md — new runbook with symptom, root cause, automated recovery command, and full manual fallback steps for debugging the automation itself.

title: Provision tank/llm-models ZFS dataset and mount on GPU node
description:
Move LLM model storage off the ssd3 LV and onto a dedicated ZFS dataset on the `tank` HDD pool (14.5 TiB total, ~12.6 TiB free). LLM serving is read-only, sequential, and intermittent — a near-ideal fit for spinning disks + ZFS ARC. This also frees the upcoming SSD flash pool (formed from ssd2/ssd3 once the new SATA adapters are installed — see home-infra-sbd) for exclusive Longhorn use.

Cold load tradeoff: a 25 GiB Q6_K model takes ~2-3 min from HDD cold cache vs ~50 s from SATA SSD; after first load it lives in ARC at RAM speed. With llama-swap's 300 s TTL, swap-thrash will cost the cold load time but inference itself never touches disk.

User will redownload all 9 GGUFs (~205 GiB total) from Hugging Face into the new dataset.
design:
On atlas:
  zfs create -o recordsize=1M -o compression=lz4 -o atime=off tank/llm-models
  zfs set xattr=sa tank/llm-models

recordsize=1M improves sequential throughput for big GGUFs (default 128K is wasteful for files this size). compression=lz4 is essentially free; GGUFs barely compress but the codepath is fast. atime=off avoids spurious writes on read.

Expose to VM 107 (GPU node, k3s-prod-worker-gpu-1) via either:
  Option A — virtio-fs passthrough: faster (no NFS overhead), more setup. Add to VM config as `args: -object memory-backend-file...` etc, or use Proxmox's experimental virtiofs.
  Option B — NFS export from atlas: simpler, mature, decent throughput (~110-150 MB/s). atlas already serves other NFS to the VMs. Add to /etc/exports, mount in VM at /mnt/llm-models.

Recommendation: NFS for simplicity. The existing `argocd/manifests/llama-cpp/base/pv.yaml` is a local PV with nodeAffinity to k3s-prod-worker-gpu-1 and `local.path: /mnt/llm-models`. As long as that path exists in the VM (regardless of what backs it), the PV binds with zero IaC changes.

title: Form new SSD flash pool from healthy drives + migrate Longhorn off tank
description:
The Samsung 870 EVO drives behind LVM VGs `ssd2` and `ssd3` became unavailable around 2026-05-19 due to a FAULTY SATA ADAPTER (not drive failure). Replacement adapters are scheduled to be installed 2026-05-21.

Original plan was to use ssd3 for LLM models; that workload is being moved to tank ZFS instead (see new sibling issue for `tank/llm-models`). Once the adapters are replaced and the drives are healthy, both ssd2 and ssd3 should be repurposed as a new flash storage pool dedicated to Longhorn replicas, replacing the current `general-storage`-tagged disks.

Goals after this:
- All Longhorn data lives on the new SSD pool (low-latency, high-IOPS)
- HDD-backed tank holds LLM models + bulk VM disks + media-adjacent storage
- Clean separation of workload classes by storage tier
design:
Steps once new SATA adapters are installed:
1. Verify both drives healthy: `smartctl -a /dev/sdX` on atlas; check for SATA link errors in dmesg
2. Decide pool topology: mirror (`zpool create flash mirror /dev/sd<X> /dev/sd<Y>`) for safety or stripe (single vdev) for capacity. Given Longhorn already replicates across nodes, a striped pool gives more usable space.
3. Create ZFS pool `flash` (or similar) on atlas with both drives
4. Add Longhorn `general-storage` tag to a new disk under each worker that has flash-backed storage
5. Drain replicas from the old LVM-backed disks; once empty, remove those disks from Longhorn
6. Update Ansible role `cluster_platform` so the new disk shows up automatically on worker provision

Affects: longhorn nodes config; possibly worker VM disk attach in `terraform/stacks/k3s/atlas/prod/workers`.

title: Migrate Plex, Jellyfin, and Monitoring PVC to longhorn-redundant
description:
Three single-pod SQLite-backed apps (Grafana, Plex, Jellyfin) lacked application-layer HA and crashed hard during the 2026-05-19 ssd3 cascade when their Longhorn volumes went attached/faulted (not just attached/degraded). To raise resilience, a new `longhorn-redundant` StorageClass was added (numberOfReplicas:3, nodeSelector:general-storage, excludes the GPU worker which is I/O-stressed by transcoding + LLM workloads). Each PVC must be migrated to the new SC.

Because PVC `storageClassName` is immutable after binding, migration requires a new PVC under a transient name (`<old-pvc>-rdn`) + an rsync data copy + a deployment claimName swap.
design:
Per-app procedure (~30 min per small app, ~5 h for Jellyfin's 58 GiB at observed 3-4 MB/s):
1. Annotate source Longhorn volume with `longhorn.io/take-snapshot=pre-rdn-migration` (NFS backup safety net).
2. Disable ArgoCD self-heal on the app's Application (so manual scale-to-0 isn't reverted).
3. `kubectl scale deployment $APP --replicas=0` and wait for pods gone.
4. Create new PVC `<old>-rdn` with `storageClassName: longhorn-redundant`.
5. Apply an alpine + rsync sidecar pod mounting both PVCs at /src and /dst; `rsync -aHAX --info=progress2 /src/ /dst/`.
6. Wait for Succeeded; verify `du -sh /src /dst` matches.
7. Update IaC: rename PVC in `base/pvc.yaml`, switch `claimName` in `base/deployment.yaml`, remove any prod overlay PVC patches.
8. Commit + push; ArgoCD reconciles with the app's self-heal re-enabled.
9. Delete migration pod, old PVC, old static PV, and the orphan Longhorn volume.

Reference docs/runbook: `argocd/manifests/longhorn-redundant-sc/README.md`.

title: Decide on Proxmox migration: type=insecure
description:
/etc/pve/datacenter.cfg has no migration: key, so Proxmox defaults to 'secure' and tunnels the migration stream over SSH. On dellssf (i3-8100T, 4 threads) that encryption - not the wire - is the bottleneck, so a 2.5G link will go largely unused for migrations.

Setting 'migration: type=insecure,network=172.20.20.0/22' typically gives 2-3x faster migration but sends VM memory and disk UNENCRYPTED over the LAN.

USER DECISION REQUIRED - this is a security tradeoff, not a technical one. Reasonable on a trusted flat home LAN, but it is the user's call.

Its own description had anticipated the rest: 'Once all 7 are moved, longhorn-one-replica-flash and longhorn-one-replica-tank will have zero live PVCs and can be retired the same way as home-infra-mi4.7.'   affine/affine-storage-pvc             longhorn-one-replica-tank    N=2  worker-3, worker-gpu-1
  karakeep/karakeep-data-pvc            longhorn-one-replica-tank    N=2  worker-2, worker-3
  karakeep/karakeep-meilisearch-pvc     longhorn-one-replica-tank    N=2  worker-1, worker-3
  health-archive/health-postgres-pvc    longhorn-one-replica-flash   N=2  worker-3, worker-4  [cross-host]
  linkding/linkding-data-pvc            longhorn-one-replica-flash   N=2  worker-1, worker-4  [cross-host]
  memos/memos-data-v3-pvc               longhorn-one-replica-flash   N=2  worker-2, worker-4  [cross-host]

Both StorageClasses still declare numberOfReplicas: 1. Nothing enforces it (SC parameters apply only at provision time) so the volumes are safely at N=2, but the names now actively mislead anyone reading either the cluster or the repo.
design:
Repo references to fix alongside the PVCs: argocd/manifests/karakeep/base/pvc.yaml (2 occurrences), argocd/manifests/linkding/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml, argocd/manifests/affine/overlays/prod/kustomization.yaml (2 occurrences).

That is real destructive work on live app data for a cosmetic-ish benefit, so it is P3 and deserves an explicit cost/benefit call before executing. A legitimate alternative is to simply CORRECT the two StorageClasses' numberOfReplicas from 1 to 2 and rename nothing, leaving the misleading names as historical artefacts -- far cheaper, though it leaves 'one-replica' in the name of a two-replica class.

The 4 tank-tier PVCs sitting on two atlas nodes is NOT drift to fix here -- per mi4.8's close notes that is an accepted tradeoff because no tank tier exists on elitedesk-1, which is home-infra-mi4.2's question. If mi4.2 gives elitedesk-1 a tank tier, those 4 gain cross-host spread on their own and this migration could ride along with it.

Pairs naturally with home-infra-mi4.7 (retiring the other legacy StorageClass aliases) -- worth doing as one sweep rather than two.

title: verify-cross-pool-placement.sh never runs on a schedule
description:

title: Periodically review PBS for orphaned backup groups (prune never empties them)
description:
PBS retention policies keep N snapshots PER GROUP indefinitely and never remove the group itself, so every guest that is deleted leaves its last few snapshots behind forever. On 2026-08-14 that had accumulated to 55 orphaned groups / 212 snapshots covering guests that had not existed for one to two years.

There is no built-in PBS automation for this -- the daily prune job and daily GC both leave orphaned groups untouched. It needs a periodic human or scripted review.
design:
A simple check: list backup groups whose NEWEST snapshot is older than some threshold (say 90 days) and cross-reference against 'pvesh get /cluster/resources --type vm'. Anything with no matching live guest is a candidate for group deletion.

CRITICAL: match on guest IDENTITY, not VMID alone. This homelab recycles VMIDs heavily -- in the 2026-08-14 cleanup, old groups for Win11-VM, guac, proxyd and game-srv sat at VMIDs now belonging to cp-1, worker-4, caddy and guacamole respectively. Use the group's newest-snapshot date plus the guest name recorded in its notes, not the number.

Could be a small script under scripts/ run quarterly, or just a calendar reminder to eyeball it.
acceptance_criteria: A documented, repeatable way to find orphaned PBS groups that does not rely on VMID matching.

title: dell-sff is memory-oversubscribed and swapping under cp-3 (etcd latency)
description:
Measured 2026-08-14, right after cp-3 was live-migrated onto dellssf:

Host: Intel i3-8100T, 4 cores / 4 threads (no HT), 15 GiB RAM.
  free -h: 13 GiB used, 1.6 GiB available, 1.9 GiB ALREADY IN SWAP
  KSM pages_sharing 129265 (~505 MiB actively deduplicated to cope)
  Sum of configured guest memory: 24064 MiB (23 GiB) on a 15 GiB host.
  VMs alone account for 18.4 GiB: cp-3 8192 + haos 8192 + pbs 2048.

Impact on etcd, comparing k3s 'took too long / apply request took / slow fdatasync' warnings over the same 50-minute window:
  cp-1 (atlas):        69 warnings, worst 744 ms
  cp-3 (dellssf):     500 warnings, worst 993 ms
  cp-4 (elitedesk-1):  83 warnings, worst 985 ms

cp-3 shows ~6x the slow-request rate of its peers, with requests reaching 993 ms against etcd's 1000 ms default election timeout. That risks spurious leader elections. The guest itself is not short of memory (2.0 GiB used of 7.8, 5.7 available) -- the stall comes from the HYPERVISOR swapping the guest's pages out.

Caveat on the absolute numbers: that window also contained the migration, the cp-2 retirement and ongoing Longhorn replica rebuilds, so all three nodes are inflated. The ~6x RELATIVE gap is the signal, not the raw counts. Re-measure on a quiet cluster to confirm the steady-state figure.
design:
Root cause is straightforward oversubscription, not a Proxmox or etcd misconfiguration. Options, cheapest first:

1. Cut haos from 8192 to 4096 MiB. Home Assistant rarely needs 8 GiB and this alone takes VM memory from 18.4 to 14.3 GiB, under physical. Costs one haos restart.
2. Cut cp-3 from 8192 to 6144 (or 4096). A k3s control-plane/etcd node in an 8-node cluster is comfortable at 4-6 GiB; the guest is only using 2.0 GiB. Costs an etcd member restart, safe at 3 members with quorum 2.
3. Move something off dellssf. pbs (2 GiB) or haos could go to elitedesk-1 -- but see the elitedesk-1-storage-constrained memory, its thin pool has limited room and haos needs ~57 GiB.
4. Add physical RAM to dell-sff. It is a small-form-factor i3 box; check max supported capacity first.

Note LXC 'memory:' is a ceiling rather than a reservation, so the four CTs (~5.6 GiB configured) contribute far less real pressure than the VMs do. Focus on the VM allocations.

Related: home-infra-se6.7 (worker-5 on dell-sff) should almost certainly not proceed -- this host has no headroom for a k3s worker.
acceptance_criteria: dellssf runs with zero swap in use under normal load; cp-3's etcd slow-request rate is comparable to cp-1 and cp-4 when measured over an equivalent quiet window.
notes:
2026-08-14 LARGELY RESOLVED by Pierce's call to move guests off rather than trim haos -- which was the right instinct: haos is genuinely using 7389 MiB of its 8192, and he reports in-guest OOM already, so shrinking it would have made things worse. Ballooning is not a factor either way (haos has balloon:0 = driver disabled, cp-3 has balloon == memory), so both VMs hold fixed allocations.

The configured-vs-actual gap was the real story. Actual RSS on dellssf before the move: cp-3 3370 MiB (of 8192), haos 7389 (of 8192), pbs 2005 (of 2048), and the four CTs just 804 MiB TOTAL against 5632 configured. LXC memory is a ceiling, not a reservation, so the '23 GiB configured on a 15 GiB host' figure badly overstated the pressure.

Moved pbs (VM 147, live, 61ms downtime) and bambu-connect (CT 121) to elitedesk-1. Result: available memory 1.6 -> 3.6 GiB, and on a settled cluster cp-3's etcd slow-request rate fell from ~40 per 4min to 2 per 4min, against cp-1 at 0 and cp-4 at 0. At parity.

Important correction to this issue's original numbers: the 500-warnings-in-50-minutes figure was heavily inflated by the cp-3 migration, the cp-2 retirement and in-flight Longhorn replica rebuilds all landing in that window. Longhorn has since converged (100 healthy, all 61 worker-4 replicas running) and the honest steady-state gap is small.

Remaining, hence P3 not closed: 1.6 GiB of STALE swap is still allocated on dellssf. It is not growing and memory is stable at 3.6 GiB available -- Linux simply does not fault pages back in until touched. 'swapoff -a && swapon -a' would clear it and fits in current headroom, but is unnecessary while etcd is performing normally. Watch item: haos is the growth risk here, since it is already OOMing at 8 GiB.

Currently longhorn-redundant (and plain longhorn/longhorn-general/longhorn-singleton) have no diskSelector at all, so they freely mix flash+tank replicas for ANY app using them, including latency-sensitive ones. jellyfin-config-pvc-rdn and plex-config-pvc-rdn (both longhorn-redundant) were specifically called out as needing to be flash-only, not tank -- config/metadata DB reads should not hit spinning disk. title: Design dedicated Longhorn storage network (Multus) once 2.5G is validated
description: User wants the 1G switch (currently idle) dedicated to management/internet traffic and the 2.5G switch dedicated purely to Longhorn replica/engine sync traffic, once the elitedesk-1/dell-sff USB 2.5G adapters are cabled. Longhorn natively supports this via its 'Storage Network' setting (Multus CNI + NetworkAttachmentDefinition), which moves replica/engine traffic off the default pod network onto a dedicated NIC/subnet.
design: Requires: Multus CNI installed cluster-wide; a NetworkAttachmentDefinition for the 2.5G storage subnet; a SECOND virtual NIC on every storage-bearing node, not just elitedesk-1 -- atlas's storage VMs (worker-1/2/3, worker-gpu-1, and worker-4/elitedesk-1) would each need an additional interface bridged to the 2.5G-only network, separate from their existing vmbr0 management/pod-network NIC. Longhorn's docs note changing the storage-network setting requires all volumes to be detached/offline briefly -- needs a real maintenance window, not an inline change. Sequenced after the 2.5G physical link is cabled and validated end-to-end (home-infra-mi4.3 gives baseline timing data first).
acceptance_criteria: Explicit go/no-go decision recorded; if yes, a maintenance window is scheduled and Multus + NAD + per-node second NIC plan is written before any Longhorn setting change.
close_reason: Not worth doing - the topology makes it a no-op for bandwidth. (1) Four of the five storage-bearing k3s nodes (worker-1/2/3, gpu-1) live on atlas, so replica traffic between them never leaves the box; it is switched in-kernel by vmbr0. (2) The only cross-host Longhorn path is atlas <-> elitedesk-1, and atlas has exactly ONE 2.5G port - a dedicated storage network would have to run either on atlas's 1G onboard NICs (slower than today) or as a VLAN on the same 2.5G wire (isolation, not bandwidth). (3) Cost is high: Multus CNI, a NetworkAttachmentDefinition, a second vNIC on every storage node, and a cluster-wide volume detach to flip the storage-network setting (verified empty today). Net bandwidth gain over simply cabling 2.5G: essentially zero. Superseded by home-infra-zzbb, which gets the same 2.5x cross-host improvement from cabling alone with no cluster downtime. Closed with --force: the blocking dep on mi4.3 is moot since this is cancelled, not deferred.

title: Decide LibreChat behavior re: peer Qwen models surfaced via cluster /v1/models

title: Add a committed template/sample of pierce-pc's llama-swap config.yaml
description:
The pierce-pc llama-swap config at C:\\Users\\pierc\\llama-cpp\\config.yaml is operator-authored, not version controlled, and points at local-only GGUF model files (so it could never be reconciled by ArgoCD anyway). It contains the 6 model entries (Qwen3.6-27B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, both -hermes variants, Gemma4-31B, Gemma4-26B-A4B) with their per-model ROCm/HIP flags, ttl: 300, --metrics, etc.

If the file is lost (disk fail, accidental delete), reconstruction requires re-deriving 6 cmd blocks with quant-specific flags, paths, and the --metrics + --no-webui + --reasoning auto pattern. That's hours of work.

Action: commit a sample under docs/WSL/LLM/templates/config.example.yaml (with placeholder paths the operator substitutes) OR include a script in scripts/workstation/ that snapshots the current config.yaml to docs/WSL/LLM/templates/ on demand. Add a note in setup.md Step 2 pointing at the template.

Bonus: a Windows-side scheduled task that nightly copies config.yaml to OneDrive/Synology Drive (which pierce-pc already runs per the Startup folder probe) would be an even better DR control.

title: Install rocm-smi on pierce-pc to unblock AMD GPU metrics for instance=workstation
description:
The Grafana llama-cpp dashboard's GPU panels (util, VRAM, temperature, power) are empty for instance=workstation because pierce-pc only has the ROCm runtime DLLs bundled with the llama.cpp build (ggml-hip.dll, rocblas.dll, etc.), not the standalone ROCm SDK that provides rocm-smi.exe.

llama-swap v218+ supports AMD GPU monitoring via rocm-smi (per upstream v218 changelog: 'Add new power draw column header for rocm-smi monitoring') but silently skips the gauges when the binary is not on PATH.

Action: install AMD's ROCm SDK for Windows (~3 GiB) OR the standalone amd-smi tool, get rocm-smi.exe on the Windows PATH, restart llama-swap.exe via the Start Llama-Swap.lnk shortcut, confirm new llamaswap_gpu_* lines appear at http://pierce-pc.levangie.org:9080/metrics.

Acceptance: bash scripts/workstation/verify-setup.sh step 2 reports >8 llamaswap_* lines (currently ~8 without GPU; would be ~14 with). Grafana workstation GPU panels populate. Documented in docs/WSL/LLM/architecture.md 'Caveats and known gaps' and docs/WSL/LLM/troubleshooting.md 'GPU panels for instance=workstation are empty'.
close_reason: Upstream-blocked: llama-swap's Windows GPU monitor (internal/perf/monitor_windows.go, v223 and earlier) only supports nvidia-smi; AMD support has never existed in the Windows build. Installing rocm-smi.exe on this host would not help because llama-swap would not call it. The actual fix is mostlygeek/llama-swap PR #779 ('perf: add vendor-agnostic GPU monitoring for Windows (experimental)') by noctrex — adds D3DKMT (DirectX) + PDH (Performance Counters) backends and the new fallback chain: nvidia-smi -> D3DKMT+PDH -> ErrNoGpuTool. Tested upstream on AMD 7900XTX with ROCm; works correctly. Status as of 2026-06-13: open, under coderabbit review, not yet merged. When this lands and we winget upgrade llama-swap, GPU panels for instance=workstation will populate automatically with zero local changes. Bonus: PDH doesn't require rocm-smi.exe at all — the HIP SDK install path I originally planned is moot. See https://github.com/mostlygeek/llama-swap/pull/779

title: Convert pierce-pc workstation setup into Ansible role
description:
The pierce-pc WSL/LLM stack (in-cluster llama-cpp <-> Windows llama-swap.exe peer + WSL2 metrics sidecar) is currently captured as docs + idempotent shell/PowerShell scripts under docs/WSL/LLM/ and scripts/workstation/. This issue is to lift that into a proper Ansible role so the same setup can be applied to a second workstation, reapplied after re-imaging, and drift-detected.

Source of truth to translate from:
- docs/WSL/LLM/setup.md — the human-readable step-by-step
- scripts/workstation/install-llama-swap-windows.ps1 — Windows half
- scripts/workstation/install-metrics-sidecar-wsl.sh — WSL2 half
- scripts/workstation/verify-setup.sh — post-install gate (becomes the role's assert tasks)

Target shape (modeled on ansible/roles/lxc/ and ansible/inventories/lxc/):
- New ansible/inventories/workstations/hosts.yml with pierce-pc as the seed host
- New ansible/roles/llama_metrics/ with tasks/{main,install_llama_swap,install_sidecar,enable_linger,verify}.yml + handlers + defaults
- New ansible/playbooks/workstation-setup.yml that imports the role with per-host vars
- ansible/group_vars/workstations.yml for shared defaults (LLAMASWAP_PORT=9080, SIDECAR_PORT=9090, etc.)

Connectivity strategy:
- Ansible connects to WSL2 over SSH (port 22 inside WSL2). Cleanest because most tasks (sidecar copy, systemd_user module, loginctl) are pure Linux.
- For the Windows-native pieces (winget install, .lnk shortcut authoring, shell:Startup) use ansible.windows + community.windows collections via win_powershell. WinRM on Windows must be enabled OR shell out to powershell.exe from inside WSL2 (the install-llama-swap-windows.ps1 script does the latter already).
- Document both options in the role README.

Task split (one tasks/*.yml per logical group, matching the script boundaries):
- install_llama_swap.yml — wraps install-llama-swap-windows.ps1 (or reimplements via win_package + win_shortcut)
- install_sidecar.yml — copy module for the sidecar script, ansible.builtin.systemd_user for the unit + enable + start
- enable_linger.yml — become: true, loginctl enable-linger
- verify.yml — uri module checks mirroring the 6 steps in verify-setup.sh; fail_when on health regressions

Open questions for the implementer:
1. Does the operator have a workstations-specific Ansible vault, or fold into the existing pattern?
2. Should the role bootstrap WSL2 itself (.wslconfig networkingMode=mirrored) or assume it's pre-provisioned? Probably the latter — WSL bootstrap is one-shot and unusual.
3. Do we want a separate role for rocm-smi install to unblock GPU panels, or out-of-scope?

References / commit history that gave us this design:
- eba66de — original peer + dashboard + sidecar
- cb43756 — peer config + ScrapeConfig
- 3ab50b1 — sidecar /running parser fix (dict-shaped entries)
- addc051 — llama-swap port fix 8080 -> 9080

Acceptance:
- ansible-playbook ansible/playbooks/workstation-setup.yml --check passes against pierce-pc with zero changes (proves idempotency against a working host)
- Adding a second workstation requires only an inventory entry + the role apply
- verify-setup.sh remains the human-runnable equivalent; the role's verify.yml tasks are the same checks in Ansible form

See docs/WSL/LLM/setup.md for the full manual procedure this should automate.

title: Bring the flash disk under Ansible management
description:
Worker host_vars currently note (ansible/inventories/production/host_vars/k3s-prod-worker-1.yml:3-4):
  'scsi3 (flash zpool, 250G, /mnt/longhorn-flash) — Currently mounted via fstab outside Ansible''s purview; not managed here.'

This is asymmetric with the tank disk (managed by ansible) and a drift risk:
- If fstab drifts, Longhorn sees an incomplete disk set with no Ansible audit
- Fresh cluster rebuilds rely on a manual mount step
- Two-tier disk model is harder to reason about

Parent: home-infra-nwr. Blocked by epic2-A (slot var) and epic2-B (unified disk task) so the flash mount uses the same machinery as data + tank.
design:
Add longhorn_flash_disk_slot: 'scsi3' to ansible/group_vars/k3s_cluster.yml.

In the role's main.yml, invoke the unified longhorn-disk.yml (from epic2-B) a third time:
  - include_tasks: longhorn-disk.yml
    vars:
      disk_device: '{{ longhorn_disk_device_template | replace("{slot}", longhorn_flash_disk_slot) }}'
      disk_path: '{{ longhorn_flash_disk_path }}'
      disk_label: flash

ansible.posix.mount manages fstab idempotently, so the existing manual fstab entries should be cleanly absorbed (the mount task is a no-op if device + path + opts match).

Coordinate the rollout: stage cluster first, observe, then prod. Don't roll all 3 prod workers simultaneously — change one mount, verify Longhorn sees the disk healthy, then the next.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fresh worker rebuild produces both /mnt/longhorn-flash and /mnt/longhorn-tank from Ansible alone, no manual fstab edits
- Existing /mnt/longhorn-flash mounts on prod survive the Ansible run with no remount disruption
- fstab entries on workers are owned by Ansible (visible in the role's mount task)
- Longhorn node CR continues to report both disks healthy during and after rollout

title: Manage Longhorn settings via Helm values instead of kubectl patch loops
description:
ansible/roles/cluster_platform/tasks/longhorn-storage-config.yml:14-65 runs ~7 'kubectl patch setting ...' shell tasks for Longhorn tunables:
- default-replica-count
- storage-reserved-percentage-for-default-disk
- replica-auto-balance
- storage-over-provisioning-percentage
- replica-auto-balance-disk-pressure-percentage
- auto-salvage
- engine-replica-timeout
- replica-replenishment-wait-interval
- concurrent-replica-rebuild-per-node-limit
- snapshot-data-integrity

All with failed_when=false. Problems:
- No idempotency check (always runs even when nothing changed)
- No diff (only success/failure surfaced via the debug task)
- Silent failures hide config drift
- Settings re-applied on every run regardless of cluster state

Parent: home-infra-nwr.
design:
Surface those settings via Helm values on the Longhorn release. Use the kubernetes.core.helm Ansible module (or whatever installer the cluster_platform role currently uses for the Longhorn chart). Helm becomes source of truth; Ansible just supplies values from ansible/group_vars/k3s_cluster.yml.

This requires investigating the Longhorn chart's values.yaml structure to confirm all settings have a Helm-values path. For settings that don't, document the gap and either (a) use a Helm post-install hook, or (b) keep a single, narrow kubectl patch task with an idempotency check (compare current vs desired before patching).

Don't lump in the BackupTarget URL change (longhorn-storage-config.yml:291-294) without separate analysis — that one may need to remain a patch because the BackupTarget CR may not be Helm-managed.
acceptance_criteria:
- Zero 'kubectl patch setting' calls remain in the cluster_platform role for the settings listed above
- Helm release shows the expected values via 'helm get values longhorn -n longhorn-system'
- Longhorn UI reflects the configured tunables
- Re-running the playbook with no var changes shows 'ok' for the Helm task (no spurious changes)

title: Auto-restart llama-cpp pod on ConfigMap change (checksum annotation)
description:
ArgoCD updates the llama-swap-config ConfigMap on commit, but llama-swap (the proxy process) reads the file once at startup and caches it in memory. After a config change, the only way to pick up the new values is a Deployment rollout restart.

When this collides with a `kubectl rollout restart` triggered immediately after a `git push` (as during the 2026-05-21 ctx-size + parallel tuning session), the new pod can start BEFORE ArgoCD has synced the new ConfigMap content to the cluster — so the new pod ends up reading the OLD ConfigMap and caches that. Restart again to fix.

Standard fix: add a checksum annotation to the Deployment template that hashes the ConfigMap data. Any change to the CM changes the hash, which changes the Deployment pod template, which triggers an automatic rollout.
design:
Two options:

OPTION A (kustomize-native): use kustomize's `configMapGenerator` instead of authoring the ConfigMap manually. It produces a content-hashed name (e.g., `llama-swap-config-abc123`) on every change, and the Deployment automatically references the new name → rollout triggered.

OPTION B (annotation): keep the manual ConfigMap and add a sha256 of its data to the Deployment spec.template.metadata.annotations.checksum/config. Implemented via kustomize replacements, helm helpers, or a CI step. Simpler conceptually but more setup boilerplate.

Recommended: OPTION A. Edit argocd/manifests/llama-cpp/base/kustomization.yaml to use configMapGenerator with the existing config.yaml file body, drop base/configmap.yaml from resources, and update Deployment volume to reference the generated name.
acceptance_criteria:
- Editing config.yaml content + git push auto-triggers a deploy rollout (verify by changing a comment in the CM data and watching `kubectl get pods -n llama-cpp -w`)
- llama-swap process command-line shows the new ConfigMap values within a minute of the ArgoCD sync (no manual restart needed)
- Existing aliases/dashboard URL unaffected (no rename of the ConfigMap that breaks volume mount)

title: [bug] llama-metrics sidecar suppresses HELP/TYPE lines after the first metric
description:
The metrics sidecar (argocd/manifests/llama-cpp/base/sidecar-exporter.py) has a dedup bug in _aggregate(): it keys deduplication on (parts[1], parts[0]) where parts comes from line.split(maxsplit=2). For '# HELP llamaswap_cpu_util_percent ...' that splits to ['#', 'HELP', 'llamaswap_cpu_util_percent ...']. The dedup key becomes ('HELP', '#') which is identical for every HELP line — so only the FIRST HELP line in the response ever passes the dedup filter. Same for TYPE.

Effect: cosmetic only. Prometheus accepts metrics without HELP/TYPE, and the actual metric VALUE lines flow correctly. Verified: dashboards still populate, all 11 llamacpp:* metrics + ~8 llamaswap_* metrics arrive labeled correctly.

Fix: change the dedup key to (parts[2].split()[0], parts[1]) — i.e. (metric_name, 'HELP'|'TYPE') — so it dedupes per (metric, kind). One-line fix in argocd/manifests/llama-cpp/base/sidecar-exporter.py around line 75. After fixing, re-deploy via configmap roll on cluster AND re-copy + restart sidecar on pierce-pc (bash scripts/workstation/install-metrics-sidecar-wsl.sh).
